instruction: How should I think about ways to arrange a desk in a home office
output:
There are several ways to arrange a desk in a home office. A few guiding principles (based on the space and how you'll use your desk) can help guide you along the way. 

* If you're frequently on camera for video calls you'll want to consider what people will see in your background. Avoid clutter and too much distraction, but also feel free to use that part of the office to express yourself professionally. An interesting painting or a few professional accolades can be a good conversation starters.

* Bright windows can be great for creativity but having these directly behind you when on video calls can give you a whitewashed look that's not ideal. Ideally, a window would be in front of you to not only cast your face in a good light, but also to give you a nice view as you work. If you can't position a window on front of your desk, you could always invest in good artificial lighting (e.g., a ring light) to help with video calls. 

* Avoid having positioning your desk so your back is directly in front of the office entrance. If you have line of site to all entrances / exits you'll likely feel more in control while working, which can make you more productive. 

* Position your desk so you have easy access to everything you'd need for work. Frequently used reference materials, papers, writing supplies, etc. should all be within arms length so as not to disrupt your "flow" while working.

instruction: Given the reference text about "The New Deal", what are the "3 R's" historians refer to about the program.
input:
The New Deal was a series of programs, public work projects, financial reforms, and regulations enacted by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in the United States between 1933 and 1939. Major federal programs and agencies included the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), the Works Progress Administration (WPA), the Civil Works Administration (CWA), the Farm Security Administration (FSA), the National Industrial Recovery Act of 1933 (NIRA) and the Social Security Administration (SSA). They provided support for farmers, the unemployed, youth, and the elderly. The New Deal included new constraints and safeguards on the banking industry and efforts to re-inflate the economy after prices had fallen sharply. New Deal programs included both laws passed by Congress as well as presidential executive orders during the first term of the presidency of Franklin D. Roosevelt.

The programs focused on what historians refer to as the "3 R's": relief for the unemployed and for the poor, recovery of the economy back to normal levels, and reform of the financial system to prevent a repeat depression. The New Deal produced a political realignment, making the Democratic Party the majority (as well as the party that held the White House for seven out of the nine presidential terms from 1933 to 1969) with its base in progressive ideas, the South, big city machines and the newly empowered labor unions, and various ethnic groups. The Republicans were split, with progressive Republicans in support but conservatives opposing the entire New Deal as hostile to business and economic growth. The realignment crystallized into the New Deal coalition that dominated presidential elections into the 1960s while the opposing conservative coalition largely controlled Congress in domestic affairs from 1937 to 1964.
output:
The "3 R's" historians refer to are the following:
- Relief for the unemployed and for the poor
- Recovery of the economy back to normal levels
- Reform of the financial system to prevent a repeat depression

instruction: Based on the passage provided, what are the only two elements in the periodic table that were names after a person who was alive at the time of naming?
input: Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element with the symbol Og and atomic number 118. It was first synthesized in 2002 at the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR) in Dubna, near Moscow, Russia, by a joint team of Russian and American scientists. In December 2015, it was recognized as one of four new elements by the Joint Working Party of the international scientific bodies IUPAC and IUPAP. It was formally named on 28 November 2016. The name honors the nuclear physicist Yuri Oganessian, who played a leading role in the discovery of the heaviest elements in the periodic table. It is one of only two elements named after a person who was alive at the time of naming, the other being seaborgium, and the only element whose eponym is alive as of 2023.
output: Organesson and Seaborgium are the only two elements in the periodic table that were names after a person who was alive at the time of naming.

instruction: Given the this paragraph about the invention of transistors, why did lawyers at Bell Labs advise Shockley against filing a patent for his field-effect transistors?
input: From November 17 to December 23, 1947, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain at AT&T's Bell Labs in Murray Hill, New Jersey performed experiments and observed that when two gold point contacts were applied to a crystal of germanium, a signal was produced with the output power greater than the input. Solid State Physics Group leader William Shockley saw the potential in this, and over the next few months worked to greatly expand the knowledge of semiconductors. The term transistor was coined by John R. Pierce as a contraction of the term transresistance. According to Lillian Hoddeson and Vicki Daitch, Shockley proposed that Bell Labs' first patent for a transistor should be based on the field-effect and that he be named as the inventor. Having unearthed Julius Edgar Lilienfeld's patents that went into obscurity years earlier, lawyers at Bell Labs advised against Shockley's proposal because the idea of a field-effect transistor that used an electric field as a "grid" was not new. Instead, what Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley invented in 1947 was the first point-contact transistor. To acknowledge this accomplishment, Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain jointly received the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics "for their researches on semiconductors and their discovery of the transistor effect".
output: The idea had previously been proposed and patented by Julius Edgar Lilienfeld.

instruction: Please give me a quick overview of Franklin Roosevelt's career.
input:
Roosevelt attended Groton School, Harvard College, and Columbia Law School, going on to practice law in New York City. He won election to the New York State Senate in 1910 and then served as Assistant Secretary of the Navy under president Woodrow Wilson during World War I. Roosevelt was James M. Cox's running mate on the Democratic Party's ticket in the 1920 United States presidential election, but Cox was defeated by Republican Warren G. Harding. In 1921, Roosevelt contracted a paralytic illness that permanently paralyzed his legs. He returned to public office by winning the 1928 New York gubernatorial election. He served as governor of New York from 1929 to 1933, promoting programs to combat the Great Depression besetting the United States at the time. In the 1932 presidential election, Roosevelt defeated Republican incumbent president Herbert Hoover in a landslide.

During his first 100 days as president, Roosevelt spearheaded unprecedented federal legislation and issued a profusion of executive orders that instituted the New Deal. He created numerous programs to provide relief to the unemployed and farmers while seeking economic recovery with the National Recovery Administration and other programs. He also instituted major regulatory reforms related to finance, communications, and labor, and presided over the end of Prohibition. In 1936, Roosevelt won a landslide reelection with the economy having improved rapidly from 1933, but the economy relapsed into a deep recession in 1937 and 1938. Later, Roosevelt unsuccessfully sought passage of the Judicial Procedures Reform Bill of 1937. The conservative coalition formed in 1937 to block the implementation of further New Deal programs and reforms. He ran successfully for reelection in 1940, becoming the only American president to serve for more than two terms.

With World War II looming after 1938 in addition to the Japanese invasion of China and the aggression of Nazi Germany, Roosevelt gave strong diplomatic and financial support to China as well as the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union while the United States remained officially neutral. Following the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, he obtained a declaration of war on Japan the next day, and a few days later, on Germany and Italy. He worked closely with other national leaders in leading the Allies against the Axis powers. Roosevelt supervised the mobilization of the American economy to support the war effort and implemented a Europe first strategy. He also initiated the development of the world's first atomic bomb and worked with the other Allied leaders to lay the groundwork for the United Nations and other post-war institutions. He won reelection in 1944 but with his physical health seriously and steadily declining during the war years, he died in 1945. Since his death, several of Roosevelt's actions have come under substantial criticism, such as his ordering of the incarceration of Japanese Americans in concentration camps. Nonetheless, historical rankings consistently rank Roosevelt as one of the greatest presidents in American history.
output: Franklin Delano Roosevelt was an American statesman and political leader who served as the 32nd president of the United States from 1933 until his death in 1945. He previously served as the 44th governor of New York from 1929 to 1933, the Assistant Secretary of the Navy from 1913 to 1920, and a member of the New York State Senate from 1911 to 1913.

instruction: Can you explain MITRE ATT&CK technique T1541 and describe how defenders detect it?
input: Technique: T1541 - Foreground Persistence
output:
**Technique:** ATT&CK T1541 - Foreground Persistence 
**Tactics:** Defense Evasion, Persistence 
**Affected Platform:** Android 

Adversaries can exploit Android's `startForeground()` API to keep continuous access to device sensors. Beginning with Android 9, background applications that are idle lose permission to use sensors such as the camera, microphone, and gyroscope. By running in the foreground - signaled via `startForeground()` - an application tells the system that a user is actively interacting with it, preventing termination. The sole requirement for initiating a foreground service is displaying a persistent notification to the user.

**Detection Guidance:** 
- **Data Source:** MobileEDR telemetry. 
- Correlate the start or promotion of a foreground service with the appearance of a persistent notification, prolonged application execution, and ongoing access to sensors (camera, microphone, location) or network activity that occurs outside expected user-driven contexts. 
- The analytic should flag applications that invoke foreground service APIs, maintain a foreground state longer than anticipated for their declared role, and retain sensor or network access while the device is locked.

**Mitigation:** 
- **ATT&CK Mitigation M1011 - User Guidance.**

instruction: Describe CWE-307's weakness and detail how developers can prevent it.
input: CWE: CWE-307 — Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
output:
The product exhibits a weakness identified as **CWE-307 - Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts**. This flaw arises because the system fails to enforce adequate controls against repeated failed login attempts within a short period.

### Impact
If exploited, an attacker can conduct unlimited authentication attempts using various passwords, ultimately achieving account compromise through brute-force methods. The vulnerability falls under **Access Control -> Bypass Protection Mechanism**, aligning with OWASP Top 10 2021 category **A07:2021**.

### Recommended Mitigations
To remediate CWE-307, implement a layered defense that includes:
- Disconnecting the user after a limited number of consecutive failures.
- Enforcing a timeout period before subsequent attempts are allowed.
- Locking out the targeted account after repeated failures.
- Requiring a computational challenge (e.g., CAPTCHA) from the user.

Prefer using well-tested libraries or frameworks that inherently guard against this weakness. Examples include authentication modules in **OpenSSL** or the **ESAPI Authenticator** ([REF-45]). Adopting such vetted components can simplify compliance with the mitigation strategy outlined in [REF-1482].

### Verification
Developers should audit code for CWE-307 patterns during both design and code-review phases. A defense-in-depth approach, coupled with rigorous security testing before deployment, will confirm that the mitigations effectively eliminate the vulnerability.

instruction: What methods do honeypots and honeytokens use to identify attacks that exploit MITRE ATT&CK technique T1047, Windows Management Instrumentation?
input: Technique to deceive/detect: T1047 - Windows Management Instrumentation (Execution)
output:
Adversaries frequently leverage Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute malicious commands and payloads, exploiting the feature's intended purpose as a uniform management interface for Windows systems. To detect this activity with high fidelity and minimal false positives, a deception strategy can be employed that incorporates decoy assets and honeytokens designed specifically to trigger alerts when WMI is used.

Key components of the approach include:

* **Honeytokens** - fabricated credentials, files, or keys that are deliberately placed in locations where legitimate use is impossible. Any interaction with these tokens indicates compromise.
* **Honeypot/decoy hosts** - virtual or isolated machines that mimic real infrastructure but contain no legitimate value. Adversaries interacting with these hosts reveal their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
* **Canary tokens** - embedded tripwires within genuine systems that generate immediate alerts when accessed.

When an adversary attempts to employ WMI for execution (T1047), the presence of these deception elements ensures a high-fidelity alert is raised, allowing defenders to respond swiftly while maintaining near-zero false positives.

instruction: I'm looking into our recent audit findings - specifically the one flagged as CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization). Which OWASP Top 10 2021 category does this fall under, and what remediation steps should we apply?
input: Weakness: CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization)
output:
CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization is a critical vulnerability that aligns with OWASP Top 10 2021 category A01:2021. The issue arises when a product performs an authorization check during an actor's attempt to access a resource or execute an action, yet the check is implemented incorrectly, allowing unauthorized access.

**Mitigation Recommendations**

- **Segregate Product Areas:** Partition the application into anonymous, normal, privileged, and administrative zones. Map roles to data and functionality meticulously to shrink the attack surface. Employ role-based access control (RBAC) [REF-229] at appropriate boundaries; however, note that RBAC alone does not guard against horizontal privilege escalation.

- **Business-Logic-Specific Checks:** Ensure that access controls tied to business logic are enforced separately from generic resource checks (files, connections, processes, memory, database records). For instance, a database might restrict medical record access to a specific user, but each individual record may have its own access constraints.

- **Use Trusted Libraries/Frameworks:** Adopt vetted authorization libraries or frameworks that inherently prevent this weakness or simplify its avoidance. Examples include the JAAS Authorization Framework [REF-233] and the OWASP ESAPI Access Control feature [REF-45].

- **Server-Side Enforcement for Web Apps:** Verify that access control is enforced on every page at the server side. Users must not gain unauthorized functionality or data by directly requesting a protected page. Techniques such as disabling caching of sensitive pages and restricting access to requests from authenticated sessions help achieve this.

Addressing CWE-863 requires applying these mitigations, validating coverage against the scenarios outlined in OWASP A01:2021, and employing both automated SAST/DAST tools and manual code review to confirm that the weakness has been eliminated.

instruction: Define the Engage goal "Prepare" and identify the approaches that support it.

Engage goal SGO0001: Prepare

Prepare ensures that the defender drives adversary engagement operations towards a desired end-state or Strategic Goal. To do so, the defender must first develop a clear understanding of their organization and the threat landscape. This includes assessing their current security posture, including known strengths and weaknesses, and inventorying priority cyber assets, including key intellectual property. These assessments and models should help the defender identify a strategic goal, with all subsequent activities aligned to it. Once a goal is selected, the defender should plan the operation by identifying a target adversary, creating the necessary Personas, and developing an operational storyboard. Key stakeholders should also establish rules for operational safety and acceptable risk. Throughout planning, the defender should incorporate intelligence from previous operations so future operations can run more effectively and efficiently.

Engage defines a single approach to make progress towards the Prepare goal: Plan. Planning brings together existing intelligence sources to inform the selection of a strategic goal and drive progress towards it. Prepare has only one approach, a deliberate focus for the first release of Engage.

Engage emphasizes that denial, deception, and adversary engagement activities cannot be treated as "fire and forget." Unlike many defensive technologies, these activities must be considered in the context of how they inform and advance larger strategic goals. Prepare helps ensure that every action in an engagement operation contributes to a unified goal.

instruction: Who is Mariano Sánchez?
input:
Mariano Sánchez Martínez (born 28 January 1978) is a Spanish former professional footballer who played as a defensive midfielder.

He appeared in 108 Segunda División games over three seasons, scoring two goals for Cartagena.

Club career
Born in San Pedro del Pinatar, Region of Murcia, Sánchez did not reach the Segunda División B until he was 26, in 2004, arriving at CD Alcoyano from amateurs AD Mar Menor-San Javier. In the following year he moved to another club at that level, FC Cartagena, helping it promote to Segunda División in his fourth season.

Sánchez made his debut in the competition on 29 August 2009 at the age of 31 years and seven months, playing the full 90 minutes in a 1–0 away win against Girona FC. He scored his first league goal on 22 May 2010 in the 3–5 home loss to Levante UD, and never appeared in less than 34 league matches during his three seasons in that tier, suffering relegation in his last and renewing his contract for a further two years in June 2012.

On 14 May 2014, the 36-year-old Sánchez announced he would retire at the end of the campaign while hoping to help his team promote, which eventually did not befell.

Personal life
Sánchez rejected an offer to play youth football for Real Murcia when he was 18, after deciding to move to Madrid to study architecture. Not being able to enter Real Madrid's youth system, he chose to retire from football.

After his playing days, Sánchez continued to work as an architect. Still as an active player, he was the figurehead behind the creation of the sports complex Pinatar Arena, in his hometown.

instruction: What kind of espresso machine is best for home use?
output:
Home espresso machines are a growing segment of the small kitchen appliance market. A good home espresso machine provides the ability to make high quality espresso in a machine that is typically smaller and less expensive than their commercial counterparts. 

There are three common espresso machine designs for home use: manual, semi-automatic, and fully automatic. As the name implies -- manual machines require direct "manual" control by the user, who typically applies pressure through a lever to deliver the desired brew pressure. Semi-automatic machines require the user to prepare the coffee into the portafilter, but then rely on an automated pump and to deliver the desired brew pressure for espresso. Fully automatic machines automate the entire process end-to-end: grinding the beans, loading the ground beans into the portafilter, and then pumping water through the portafilter at predefined pressure levels to brew espresso. 

Manual machines typically have a lower cost, smaller footprint, and provide the user with more direct control over the brewing process. This allows skilled users to make higher-quality espresso than they would with a more automated machine. In contrast, fully automatic machines are often the easiest to use, but are unable to make espresso as consistently great as a skilled barista could with a manual machines. Fully automatic machines are inherently more complex, more expensive to purchase, and more likely to have longer-term reliability issues. 

Regardless of the type of espresso machine, two factors influence how well they will perform: their ability to manage brew temperature and brew pressure. The best machines provide the ability to vary brew temperature and pressure in consistent, repeatable ways.The type of coffee bean and desired result will impact what temperature and pressure profile the user wants. The best machines offer flexibility along both dimensions in consistent, repeatable ways.

The identified weakness is **CWE-652 - Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions (XQuery Injection)**. - **Impact:** Read Application Data - an adversary could access sensitive content stored in the XML database.

**OWASP Top 10 2021 Correlation**

- This weakness maps to **A03:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures**.

Developers should audit code for CWE-652 patterns during both design and code-review stages, implement the above mitigations as part of a defense-in-depth strategy, and verify coverage through comprehensive security testing before deployment.

instruction: How was art used for manipulative purpose in racial discuss in the 20th century?
input: Racial categories have historically been used as a way to enable an oppressive figure or group to discriminate against other groups or individuals which were seen as different from that of the oppressor. In nineteenth and early twentieth century Europe, artwork was a common form of racialization which targeted countries in the Middle East and Asia. The artwork, predominantly paintings, were portrayed in order to instill prejudice in the Western populations through sexualizing and manipulating images. One of the most prominent examples of Orientalist work in art is a piece by Eugène Delacroix titled Women of Algiers in their Apartment. Dating back to 1834, it portrays three women resting in a harem in exotic clothing while an African woman is dressed in plain clothing, depicting her role as a servant. Fine textiles, hookahs, and other paraphernalia adorn the room, which represents a European fantasy of an exotic scene. Attempts to portray these cultures as strange, foreign and exotic through Orientalism led to intolerance towards the Arab and Asian communities in Europe and the United States. Others argue that Delacroix, who travelled in North Africa sketching extensively, was depicting a realistic scene of the era based on his first-hand knowledge and experience. In such an interpretation the clothing, for example, is consistent with the times, as Arab North Africans dressed differently from Europeans, and kept black slaves who would not have been treated as equals.
output: In the 19th to 20th century, Europeans commonly use artworks to portray prejudice towards Middle Eastern and Asian people.

instruction: Given this reference text about the Grateful Dead, tell me who their keyboard players were over the years.
input: The Grateful Dead was founded in the San Francisco Bay Area amid the rise of the counterculture of the 1960s. The founding members were Jerry Garcia (lead guitar, vocals), Bob Weir (rhythm guitar, vocals), Ron "Pigpen" McKernan (keyboards, harmonica, vocals), Phil Lesh (bass, vocals), and Bill Kreutzmann (drums). Members of the Grateful Dead, originally known as the Warlocks, had played together in various Bay Area ensembles, including the traditional jug band Mother McCree's Uptown Jug Champions. Lesh was the last member to join the Warlocks before they changed their name to the Grateful Dead; replacing Dana Morgan Jr., who had played bass for a few gigs. Drummer Mickey Hart and non-performing lyricist Robert Hunter joined in 1967. With the exception of McKernan, who died in 1973, and Hart, who took time off from 1971 to 1974, the core of the band stayed together for its entire 30-year history. The other official members of the band are Tom Constanten (keyboards; 1968–1970), John Perry Barlow (non-performing lyricist; 1971–1995), Keith Godchaux (keyboards, occasional vocals; 1971–1979), Donna Godchaux (vocals; 1972–1979), Brent Mydland (keyboards, vocals; 1979–1990), and Vince Welnick (keyboards, vocals; 1990–1995). Bruce Hornsby (accordion, piano, vocals) was a touring member from 1990 to 1992, as well as a guest with the band on occasion before and after the tours.
output: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan was the original keyboard player of the Grateful Dead. Others to play keyboards for the Grateful Dead include Tom Constanten, Keith Godchaux, Brent Mydland and Vince Welnick.

**Threat Hunt - T1615 Group Policy Discovery**

**Objective** 
Identify adversary activity that enumerates Group Policy settings within the environment.

**Data Sources** 
- NSM:Flow 
- WinEventLog:PowerShell 
- WinEventLog:Security 
- WinEventLog:Sysmon 

**Detection Guidance** 
Adversaries typically use one or more of the following methods to discover Group Policy objects:

1. **Command-line enumeration** - execution of `gpresult` or similar utilities that return policy details. 
2. **PowerShell discovery** - scripts invoking cmdlets such as `Get-DomainGPO`, `Get-DomainGPOLocalGroup`, or other custom PowerShell modules designed to pull GPO information. 
3. **LDAP queries** - abnormal LDAP requests targeting objects within the `groupPolicyContainer` naming context, often with filters that enumerate all policy objects.

Defenders should look for: 
- Unusual process lineage indicating a chain of scripts or binaries culminating in one of the above commands. 
- Script execution events (PowerShell) that reference GPO-related cmdlets or custom modules. 
- LDAP filter activity against domain controllers that references `groupPolicyContainer` objects.

**Pivot Strategy** 
When a confirmed hit is identified, scope the event to the specific host, account, and time window involved. From there, map any adjacent techniques within the same tactic chain (Discovery) to build a comprehensive view of the adversary's reconnaissance activity.

instruction: Provide a supply-chain risk assessment for GHSA-6chq-wfr3-2hj9 in the 'axios' library.
input: OSV ID: GHSA-6chq-wfr3-2hj9  |  Package: axios (npm)
output:
**Supply-Chain Vulnerability - GHSA-6chq-wfr3-2hj9**

*Package:* **axios** (npm ecosystem) 
*Also tracked as:* **CVE-2026-42035** 
*Severity:* LOW 

**Affected version ranges** 
- >= 1.0.0, < 1.15.1 
- >= 0, < 0.31.1 

**Fixed in** 
- 1.15.1 
- 0.31.1 

---

### Vulnerability Summary
Axios' HTTP adapter (lib/adapters/http.js) contains a prototype-pollution gadget that permits an attacker to inject arbitrary HTTP headers into outgoing requests. The flaw arises from duck-type checking of the data payload: if `Object.prototype` is polluted with methods such as `getHeaders`, `append`, `pipe`, `on`, `once`, and `Symbol.toStringTag`, Axios mistakenly treats any plain object payload as a FormData instance and invokes the attacker-controlled `getHeaders()` function. The headers returned by this function are then merged into the request, enabling header injection.

### Supply-Chain Impact
Any project that directly or transitively depends on **axios** within the affected version ranges is exposed. Because axios is widely used across the npm ecosystem, a single unpatched instance can propagate this vulnerability throughout an entire application graph without downstream consumers' explicit awareness.

### Recommended Action
- Pin or upgrade **axios** to a non-affected release (>= 1.15.1 or >= 0.31.1). 
- Audit dependency lock files and CI/CD pipelines to ensure the fixed version is resolved both transitively and directly. 

**Advisory URL:** https://github.com/axios/axios/security/advisories/GHSA-6chq-wfr3-2hj9

instruction: Determine the potential blast radius across the RubyGems ecosystem if an attacker exploits GHSA-p543-xpfm-54cp in rack.

**Vulnerability Overview**

* **ID:** GHSA-p543-xpfm-54cp 
* **Affected Component:** `rack` (RubyGems) 
* **Severity:** LOW 

**Version Impacted**

The vulnerability exists in the following version ranges:

- `>=0,<2.2.19`
- `>=3.1,<3.1.17`
- `>=3.2,<3.2.2`

**Technical Summary**

Rack's unbounded multipart preamble buffering allows an attacker to trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition through memory exhaustion.

**Supply-Chain Blast Radius**

The `rack` gem is widely used as a dependency across the RubyGems ecosystem. Any downstream package or application that resolves an affected version - whether directly or via deeply nested transitive dependencies - can silently inherit this vulnerability, often without maintainers' awareness.

**Attack Surface Dimensions**

1. **Direct dependents:** Projects that explicitly list `rack` in their manifest within the affected version constraints. 
2. **Transitive dependents:** Projects that pull `rack` indirectly through other libraries; these constitute the majority of exposed consumers. 
3. **CI/CD and build tooling:** Build pipelines that install dependencies at build time are also exposed if they resolve an affected version. 
4. **Container images:** Base images bundling affected versions propagate exposure to every image layer built on top.

**Mitigation Recommendations**

- **Registry maintainers:** Consider yanking or flagging the affected `rack` versions. 
- **Dependents:** Upgrade to a fixed release - `2.2.19`, `3.1.17`, or `3.2.2`. 
- **Organizations:** Enforce dependency scanning in CI pipelines to detect and prevent re-introduction of vulnerable versions.

**Advisory Reference**

For full details, see the official advisory: https://github.com/rack/rack/security/advisories/GHSA-p543-xpfm-54cp

This field can trace its roots to processes of European colonization and globalization, when European trade with other parts of the world and eventual political control of overseas territories offered scholars access to different cultures. Anthropology was the scientific discipline that searches to understand human diversity, both culturally and biologically. Originally anthropology focused on understanding groups of people then considered "primitive" or "simple" whereas sociology focused on modern urban societies in Europe and North America although more recently cultural anthropology looks at all cultures around the world, including those in developed countries. Over the years, sociocultural anthropology has influenced other disciplines like urban studies, gender studies, ethnic studies and has developed a number of sub-disciplines like medical anthropology, political anthropology, environmental anthropology, applied anthropology, psychological anthropology, economic anthropology and others have developed.
output: Ethnology can trace its roots to European colonization and globalization.

instruction: Given a reference text about a former President of India, Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, tell me when he was born, where he was raised and the subjects he specialised in studies. Why was Abdul Kalam known as the Missile Man of India?
input:
Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam BR (/ˈɑːbdəl kəˈlɑːm/ (listen); 15 October 1931 – 27 July 2015) was an Indian aerospace scientist and statesman who served as the 11th president of India from 2002 to 2007. He was born and raised in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu and studied physics and aerospace engineering. He spent the next four decades as a scientist and science administrator, mainly at the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and was intimately involved in India's civilian space programme and military missile development efforts. He thus came to be known as the Missile Man of India for his work on the development of ballistic missile and launch vehicle technology. He also played a pivotal organisational, technical, and political role in India's Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998, the first since the original nuclear test by India in 1974.

Kalam was elected as the 11th president of India in 2002 with the support of both the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party and the then-opposition Indian National Congress. Widely referred to as the "People's President", he returned to his civilian life of education, writing and public service after a single term. He was a recipient of several prestigious awards, including the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour.
output:
Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam BR, referred to as APJ Abdul Kalam in short, was born on 15th October 1931. He was born and raised in Rameswaram in Tamil Nadu, South India. APJ Abdul Kalam specialised in Physics and Aerospace Engineering as part of his studies. 
He had a career of around 4 decades as a scientist as well as an administrator with the organisations such as Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). In these roles, APJ Abdul Kalam played a key role in India's civilian space program and military missile development activities. He also played a vital role in the development of ballistic missile and launch vehicle technology. As a result of his above mentioned contributions, Abdul Kalam was known as the Missile Man of India.

instruction: Who are the little Japanese girls who find Totoro?
input: In 1950s Japan, university professor Tatsuo Kusakabe and his daughters Satsuki and Mei (approximately ten and four years old, respectively) move into an old house close to the hospital where the girls' mother Yasuko is recovering from a long-term illness. The house is inhabited by small, dark, dust-like house spirits called susuwatari, which can be seen when moving from bright places to dark ones.[note 1] When the girls become comfortable in their new house, the susuwatari leave to find another empty house. Mei later discovers two small spirits who lead her into the hollow of a large camphor tree. She befriends a larger spirit, which identifies itself using a series of roars she interprets as "Totoro". Mei thinks Totoro is the troll from her illustrated book Three Billy Goats Gruff, with her mispronouncing troll. Mei falls asleep atop Totoro but when Satsuki finds her, she is on the ground. Despite many attempts, Mei cannot show her family Totoro's tree. Tatsuo comforts her by telling her Totoro will reveal himself when he wants to.
output: Mei and Satsuki are the two Japanese girls who discover Totoro in the famous Japanese anime My Neighbour Totoro.

instruction: Since GHSA-w9j2-pvgh-6h63 affects the popular 'axios' npm package, can you explain the blast radius of a supply-chain compromise in this context?
input: Ecosystem: npm  |  Package: axios  |  OSV: GHSA-w9j2-pvgh-6h63
output:
**Blast Radius Analysis - GHSA-w9j2-pvgh-6h63 (npm/axios)** 

**Severity:** LOW 
**Affected version ranges:** 
- `>=1.0.0,<1.15.1` 
- `>=0,<0.31.1`

**Vulnerability Summary** 
Axios is vulnerable to an **Authentication Bypass via Prototype Pollution Gadget in the `validateStatus` Merge Strategy**. This flaw allows an attacker to manipulate prototype properties, potentially bypassing authentication checks.

**Supply-Chain Blast Radius** 
The npm package `axios` is widely used as a dependency across numerous downstream packages and applications. A vulnerability in any affected version of `{pkg}` propagates silently through every dependent project that resolves that version - including deeply nested transitive dependencies that maintainers may not be aware of.

**Attack Surface Dimensions** 

- **Direct dependents:** Any project that explicitly lists `axios` in its manifest within the affected version constraint. 
- **Transitive dependents:** Projects that pull `axios` indirectly via other libraries - the majority of exposed consumers. 
- **CI/CD and build tooling:** Build pipelines that install dependencies at build time are also exposed if they resolve an affected version. 
- **Container images:** Base images that bundle affected versions propagate exposure to every image layer built on top.

**Recommended Containment** 

1. Registry maintainers should consider yanking or flagging the affected versions. 
2. Dependents should upgrade to a fixed release: `1.15.1` or `0.31.1`. 
3. Organizations should enforce dependency scanning in CI to catch re-introductions.

**Advisory URL:** https://github.com/axios/axios/security/advisories/GHSA-w9j2-pvgh-6h63

instruction: Could you analyze ATT&CK technique T1685 (Disable or Modify Tools) within the realm of cloud/SaaS security?
input: Technique: T1685 - Disable or Modify Tools  | environment: cloud / SaaS
output:
**Threat Analysis - T1685: Disable or Modify Tools**

Adversaries targeting cloud and SaaS environments may seek to impair defensive visibility by disabling, degrading, or tampering with security tools and applications. Typical targets include endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions, intrusion detection systems (IDS), antivirus engines, logging agents, sensors, and other monitoring utilities. Attack techniques can involve stopping specific services, terminating processes, altering or deleting configuration files, modifying Registry keys, or otherwise preventing these tools from functioning.

**Platforms Affected:** Containers, ESXi, IaaS, Linux, macOS

**Detection Recommendations for Cloud/SaaS Deployments**

- **AWS CloudTrail** - Monitor API activity that could indicate tampering with security services. 
- **Windows Event Log: Sysmon** - Capture process creation and termination events. 
- **Windows Event Log: System** - Observe service start/stop actions. 
- **auditd: CONFIG_CHANGE** - Detect configuration file modifications on Linux hosts. 
- **auditd: SYSCALL** - Identify system calls that may reflect tampering or privilege escalation.

**Mitigation Controls**

1. **M1018 User Account Management** - Enforce least-privilege and strong authentication to limit the ability of adversaries to modify security tools. 
2. **M1047 Audit** - Enable comprehensive logging for all security-relevant actions. 
3. **M1022 Restrict File and Directory Permissions** - Protect configuration files and binaries from unauthorized changes. 
4. **M1042 Disable or Remove Feature or Program** - Ensure that only approved tools are installed and running; disable or uninstall unused components. 
5. **M1054 Software Configuration** - Harden security tool settings to resist tampering, including integrity checks and signed configurations.

By combining vigilant monitoring with these mitigations, organizations can reduce the risk of adversaries successfully disabling or modifying their defensive tooling in cloud and SaaS environments.

instruction: From the passage list down the location of Visa data centers. List the results in semi colon separated format.
input:
Visa Inc. (/ˈviːzə, ˈviːsə/; stylized as VISA) is an American multinational financial services corporation headquartered in San Francisco, California. It facilitates electronic funds transfers throughout the world, most commonly through Visa-branded credit cards, debit cards and prepaid cards. Visa is one of the world's most valuable companies.

Visa does not issue cards, extend credit or set rates and fees for consumers; rather, Visa provides financial institutions with Visa-branded payment products that they then use to offer credit, debit, prepaid and cash access programs to their customers. In 2015, the Nilson Report, a publication that tracks the credit card industry, found that Visa's global network (known as VisaNet) processed 100 billion transactions during 2014 with a total volume of US$6.8 trillion.

Visa was founded in 1958 by Bank of America (BofA) as the BankAmericard credit card program. In response to competitor Master Charge (now Mastercard), BofA began to license the BankAmericard program to other financial institutions in 1966. By 1970, BofA gave up direct control of the BankAmericard program, forming a cooperative with the other various BankAmericard issuer banks to take over its management. It was then renamed Visa in 1976.

Nearly all Visa transactions worldwide are processed through the company's directly operated VisaNet at one of four secure data centers, located in Ashburn, Virginia; Highlands Ranch, Colorado; London, England; and Singapore. These facilities are heavily secured against natural disasters, crime, and terrorism; can operate independently of each other and from external utilities if necessary; and can handle up to 30,000 simultaneous transactions and up to 100 billion computations every second.

Visa is the world's second-largest card payment organization (debit and credit cards combined), after being surpassed by China UnionPay in 2015, based on annual value of card payments transacted and number of issued cards. However, because UnionPay's size is based primarily on the size of its domestic market in China, Visa is still considered the dominant bankcard company in the rest of the world, where it commands a 50% market share of total card payments.
output: Ashburn, Virginia; Highlands Ranch, Colorado; London, England; Singapore

instruction: Explain how a malicious insider might abuse T1567 and describe the techniques for detecting such activity.

Supply-Chain Vulnerability: GHSA-2655-q453-22f9

- LOW 

**Affected Versions** 
- >=1.3,<1.3.4 
- >=1.4,<1.4.2 

**Fixed In** 
- 1.3.4, 1.4.2 

### Vulnerability Summary
The `django.http.HttpRequest.get_host` function in Django versions 1.3.x before 1.3.4 and 1.4.x before 1.4.2 allows remote attackers to generate and display arbitrary URLs via crafted username and password Host header values.

### Supply-Chain Impact
Any project that directly or transitively depends on the affected `django` package is exposed. Because Django is widely used as a dependency in the PyPI ecosystem, an unpatched version can propagate this vulnerability throughout an entire application graph without explicit awareness from downstream consumers.

- Pin or upgrade `django` to a non-affected release (1.3.4 or 1.4.2). 
- Audit your dependency lock files and CI/CD pipelines to confirm that the fixed version is resolved both transitively and directly.

instruction: Why is the sky blue?
output:
Because the Earth's atmosphere scatters the light of the sun, and blue light scatters more readily than other colors in the spectrum, we tend to see the sky as blue.

Light can be affected by the medium it passes through. For example, a prism separates white light into a spectrum of colors, and a mirror reflects the light entirely. When it passes through the atmosphere, light gets scattered. If unimpeded, the light of the sun is white.

Blue light has a shorter wavelength than other colors of light, and it scatters more easily. It is this scattering which makes it perceptible to the human eye.When the sun starts to set, the light is passing through even more atmosphere, and yet further colors are visible (such as orange and red).

You can read more at https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/blue-sky/en/, where I researched this answer.

instruction: What is Cup Game?
input: The cup game is a children's clapping game that involves tapping and hitting a cup using a defined rhythm.
output: The cup game is a children's clapping game that involves tapping and hitting a cup using a defined rhythm. The game can be played by many players seated around a table and is often played in large groups. Each player possesses a cup and in unison the players tap out the defined rhythm using their cups. It can be played competitively, where the rhythm speeds up in each "round", and a player making a mistake in the rhythm must drop out of the game, with a new "round" starting after each elimination, and game play continuing until only one player remains, with that player being the winner.

instruction: In the context of Engage goals, what does "Understand" mean, and which approaches support it?
input: Engage goal: SGO0002 Understand
output:
Engage goal SGO0002, Understand, focuses on collecting and synthesizing raw operational outputs to inform future operations and defensive strategies. It helps defenders assess progress toward Strategic Goals by connecting operational results to the broader strategy and turning them into useful, actionable intelligence.

Operational outputs may include collected PCAP, logs, and qualitative defender observations. Applying analytics can map this data to adversary behavior, provide context for the intelligence, and inform the existing threat model. For example, a defender may identify a new IP address used for exfiltration in raw PCAP data and add it to the threat model. Behavioral analysis may also reveal a new Defense Evasion technique, which should be incorporated into the threat model. Defenders should then assess whether the new intelligence affects ongoing operations, including whether current collection efforts can detect the new TTP.

Post-operation analysis can also help refine individual engagement activities based on qualitative and quantitative outputs. Defenders can review how the engagement went and adjust future activities to maximize their usefulness. They should also assess coordination and communication, seeking to improve teamwork and skills with each operation.

Engage defines one approach to advance the Understand goal: Analyze. This single approach is intentional for the first release of Engage. Denial, deception, and adversary engagement activities should not be treated as "fire and forget." They must be considered in the context of how they inform and advance larger strategic goals. Analysis turns raw operational outputs into intelligence that drives progress toward those goals.

instruction: Analyze the adversarial-ML incident described in the ATLAS case study AML.CS0038.
input: ATLAS Case Study: AML.CS0038 — Planting Instructions for Delayed Automatic AI Agent Tool Invocation
output:
**Case Study: AML.CS0038 - Delayed Automatic AI Agent Tool Invocation in Google Gemini**

On **2024-02-01**, the threat group *Embrace the Red* demonstrated that Google Gemini can be coerced into invoking an AI agent tool by deferring execution to a subsequent conversation turn. This technique bypasses the platform's security control that prohibits tool invocation within the same turn in which untrusted data is introduced, thereby allowing access to sensitive user information.

**Target & Actor**

- **Target:** Google Gemini 
- **Actor:** Embrace the Red 

**Observed ATLAS Techniques**

| Technique | MITRE/ATLAS ID | Tactic |
|-----------|----------------|--------|
| LLM Prompt Crafting | AML.T0065 | Resource Development |
| Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Application | AML.T0093 | Initial Access, Persistence |
| Indirect Execution | AML.T0051.001 | Execution |
| Delay Execution of LLM Instructions | AML.T0094 | Defense Evasion |
| AI Agent Tool Invocation | AML.T0053 | Execution, Privilege Escalation |
| AI Agent Tools | AML.T0085.001 | Collection |

**Attack Flow**

1. **Prompt Crafting (AML.T0065):** The researcher authored a prompt designed to retrieve text from a private Google Doc through Gemini's Workspace Extension. 
2. **Infiltration (AML.T0093):** This malicious prompt was embedded within the body of a lengthy email sent to the victim, leveraging a public-facing application as an initial access vector. 
3. **Execution Trigger (AML.T0051.001):** When the user prompted Gemini to summarize or otherwise interact with the email, the hidden prompt executed. 
4. **Defense Evasion (AML.T0094):** The prompt instructed Gemini to delay invoking the Workspace Extension until the next interaction, thereby circumventing controls that block tool usage in the same turn as untrusted input. 
5. **Tool Invocation (AML.T0053):** Upon the victim's subsequent interaction with Gemini, the delayed Workspace Extension was activated. 
6. **Data Collection (AML.T0085.001):** The extension located the targeted document and inserted its contents into the chat context for the user.

**Mitigations from ATLAS**

- AI Telemetry Logging (AML.M0024) 
- Input and Output Validation for AI Agent Components (AML.M0033) 
- Generative AI Guardrails (AML.M0020) 
- Generative AI Guidelines (AML.M0021) 
- Generative AI Model Alignment (AML.M0022)

Implementing these mitigations can reduce the risk of delayed tool invocation attacks and help maintain control over sensitive data within generative AI environments.

instruction: Can you let me know which OWASP Top 10 2021 item corresponds to CWE-201 and walk through the controls that are required?
input: Weakness: CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data)
output:
CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

**OWASP Top 10 2021 mapping:** A01:2021 

The identified weakness occurs when the application transmits data to another actor, yet a portion of that transmitted payload contains sensitive information that should not be accessible to the receiving party.

### Mitigation Guidance (MITRE CWE)

- **Define Sensitive Data** - Clearly specify which data elements are considered sensitive and determine which user roles or actors should have access to each type. 
- **Verify Requirements with Designers** - Confirm that any potentially sensitive data identified in the requirements is either a calculated risk or mitigated elsewhere. Remove any unnecessary information to reduce both overhead and the likelihood of accidental disclosure. 
- **Default Error Messages** - Configure error handling so that unexpected errors do not leak sensitive information. 
- **Compartmentalization** - Design the system with distinct "safe" areas where trust boundaries are explicit. Prevent sensitive data from crossing these boundaries, and enforce privilege separation through appropriate compartmentalization built into the architecture.

Addressing CWE-201 requires applying the mitigations above and validating that the controls cover all scenarios described in OWASP A01:2021. Both automated SAST/DAST tools and manual code review should be employed to confirm that the weakness has been eliminated.

instruction: How can we defend against the Exploitation of Thunderbolt Protection Flaws attack pattern (CAPEC-665)?
input: Attack pattern: CAPEC-665 Exploitation of Thunderbolt Protection Flaws
output:
## Defending Against CAPEC-665: Exploitation of Thunderbolt Protection Flaws

An adversary with physical access to a target device may exploit a firmware weakness in the Thunderbolt protocol by manipulating the Thunderbolt controller firmware. The attack targets vulnerabilities in the implementation of authorization and verification schemes within Thunderbolt protection mechanisms. Typically, while the target device is booting, the adversary uses a SPI programming device and an external Thunderbolt device to manipulate the victim Thunderbolt controller's SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) flash. If successful, this may allow the adversary to modify memory, subvert authentication mechanisms, and spoof...

CAPEC lists the following mitigations:

- **Implementation:** Kernel Direct Memory Access Protection
- **Configuration:** Enable the UEFI option **USB Passthrough mode** - the Thunderbolt 3 system port operates as a USB 3.1 Type C interface.
- **Configuration:** Enable the UEFI option **DisplayPort mode** - the Thunderbolt 3 system port operates as a video-only DP interface.
- **Configuration:** Enable the UEFI option **Mixed USB/DisplayPort mode** - the Thunderbolt 3 system port operates as a USB 3.1 Type C interface with support for DP mode.

instruction: Explain CWE-515 (Covert Storage Channel) and list the controls that prevent it.
input: CWE: CWE-515 — Covert Storage Channel
output:
**Weakness:** CWE-515 - Covert Storage Channel 

**Description** 
Covert storage channels arise when out-of-band data is embedded within legitimate messages to exploit memory reuse. These channels are typically classified as either storage or timing channels. A classic example involves using a file that is intended solely for audit purposes to transmit user passwords, by encoding the password in the file name or status bits that all users can read. Steganography - concealing information so that only the intended recipient knows of its existence - is another form of covert storage channel.

**Consequences if Exploited** 
- **Confidentiality:** Attackers may read application data. 
- **Integrity & Confidentiality:** If messages or packets contain unnecessary data, malicious listeners can infer which process created the message, potentially revealing system details and aiding further attacks.

**Mitigations (MITRE CWE)** 
- Ensure that all reserved fields are set to zero before sending messages and that no extraneous information is included. 

Developers should audit code for CWE-515 patterns during design and code review, apply these mitigations in a defense-in-depth strategy, and verify coverage with security testing prior to deployment.

output:
Jorge Francisco Isidoro Luis Borges Acevedo (/ˈbɔːrhɛs/; Spanish: [ˈboɾxes] (listen); 24 August 1899 – 14 June 1986) was an Argentine short-story writer, essayist, poet and translator, as well as a key figure in Spanish-language and international literature. His best-known books, Ficciones (Fictions) and El Aleph (The Aleph), published in the 1940s, are collections of short stories exploring themes of dreams, labyrinths, chance, infinity, archives, mirrors, fictional writers and mythology. Borges's works have contributed to philosophical literature and the fantasy genre, and have had a major influence on the magic realist movement in 20th century Latin American literature.

Born in Buenos Aires, Borges later moved with his family to Switzerland in 1914, where he studied at the Collège de Genève. The family travelled widely in Europe, including Spain. On his return to Argentina in 1921, Borges began publishing his poems and essays in surrealist literary journals. He also worked as a librarian and public lecturer. In 1955, he was appointed director of the National Public Library and professor of English Literature at the University of Buenos Aires. He became completely blind by the age of 55. Scholars have suggested that his progressive blindness helped him to create innovative literary symbols through imagination.[Note 1] By the 1960s, his work was translated and published widely in the United States and Europe. Borges himself was fluent in several languages.

In 1961, he came to international attention when he received the first Formentor Prize, which he shared with Samuel Beckett. In 1971, he won the Jerusalem Prize. His international reputation was consolidated in the 1960s, aided by the growing number of English translations, the Latin American Boom, and by the success of García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude. He dedicated his final work, The Conspirators, to the city of Geneva, Switzerland. Writer and essayist J. M. Coetzee said of him: "He, more than anyone, renovated the language of fiction and thus opened the way to a remarkable generation of Spanish-American novelists."

instruction: Hey, do you know how we might leverage honeypots or honeytokens to detect ATT&CK T1020 - Automated Exfiltration?
input: Technique to deceive/detect: T1020 - Automated Exfiltration (Exfiltration)
output:
Adversaries often employ automated exfiltration (T1020) to move collected data - such as sensitive documents - to external destinations. A robust deception strategy can expose these efforts with minimal false positives by deploying decoy assets that attract and reveal the adversary's behavior.

Key deception components:

* **Honeytokens** - fake credentials, files, or cryptographic keys that are designed to appear valuable but serve no legitimate purpose. Any use of a honeytoken is an immediate indicator of compromise.
* **Honeypot/decoy hosts** - fully functional-looking systems placed within the network to lure attackers. Interaction with these decoys allows analysts to capture the adversary's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) in real time.
* **Canary tokens** - lightweight tripwires embedded directly into operational environments. When triggered, they provide early warning of unauthorized activity.

By integrating these elements, an organization can detect automated exfiltration attempts with high fidelity while keeping false-positive rates near zero.

instruction: What is linux Bootloader
input:
A bootloader, also spelled as boot loader or called boot manager and bootstrap loader, is a computer program that is responsible for booting a computer.

When a computer is turned off, its software including operating systems, application code, and data‍—‌remains stored on non-volatile memory. When the computer is powered on, it typically does not have an operating system or its loader in random-access memory (RAM). The computer first executes a relatively small program stored in read-only memory (ROM, and later EEPROM, NOR flash) along with some needed data, to initialize RAM (especially on x86 systems), to access the nonvolatile device (usually block device, eg NAND flash) or devices from which the operating system programs and data can be loaded into RAM.

Some earlier computer systems, upon receiving a boot signal from a human operator or a peripheral device, may load a very small number of fixed instructions into memory at a specific location, initialize at least one CPU, and then point the CPU to the instructions and start their execution. These instructions typically start an input operation from some peripheral device (which may be switch-selectable by the operator). Other systems may send hardware commands directly to peripheral devices or I/O controllers that cause an extremely simple input operation (such as "read sector zero of the system device into memory starting at location 1000") to be carried out, effectively loading a small number of boot loader instructions into memory; a completion signal from the I/O device may then be used to start execution of the instructions by the CPU.

Smaller computers often use less flexible but more automatic boot loader mechanisms to ensure that the computer starts quickly and with a predetermined software configuration. In many desktop computers, for example, the bootstrapping process begins with the CPU executing software contained in ROM (for example, the BIOS of an IBM PC or an IBM PC compatible) at a predefined address (some CPUs, including the Intel x86 series are designed to execute this software after reset without outside help). This software contains rudimentary functionality to search for devices eligible to participate in booting, and load a small program from a special section (most commonly the boot sector) of the most promising device, typically starting at a fixed entry point such as the start of the sector.
output: A bootloader is a program written in machine code that loads the operating system into RAM during the boot process.

Nation-state cyber operations such as those conducted by APT38 typically serve strategic objectives - espionage, pre-positioning, intellectual-property theft, or influence operations - that align with the sponsoring state's interests. Case Study: AML.CS0024 - Morris II Worm (RAG-Based Attack)

**Incident Overview**

On 2024-03-05, researchers disclosed the development of *Morris II*, a zero-click worm engineered to infiltrate generative AI (GenAI) ecosystems and self-propagate across connected GenAI systems. The worm leverages an adversarial, self-replicating prompt that employs prompt injection to both replicate itself as output and trigger malicious actions.

The proof-of-concept demonstrates propagation via a RAG-based email assistant. In this scenario the target system automatically ingests incoming emails, retrieves prior correspondence, and generates replies on behalf of the user. The researchers sent a malicious email containing the worm to an address within the target environment; once the GenAI assistant processed the message during reply generation, the worm's prompt injection altered its behavior, enabling further spread.

**Actors**

- Stav Cohen 
- Ron Bitton 
- Ben Nassi 

**Target**

RAG-based email assistant

**Observed ATLAS Techniques**

- **AML.T0040** - AI Model Inference API Access (tactic: AI Model Access) 
- **AML.T0051.000** - Direct (tactic: Execution) 
- **AML.T0053** - AI Agent Tool Invocation (tactic: Execution, Privilege Escalation) 
- **AML.T0051.002** - Triggered (tactic: Execution) 
- **AML.T0061** - LLM Prompt Self-Replication (tactic: Persistence) 
- **AML.T0057** - LLM Data Leakage (tactic: Exfiltration) 
- **AML.T0048.003** - User Harm (tactic: Impact)

**Key Attack Steps**

1. **[AML.T0040]** Researchers accessed the publicly available GenAI model API that powers the target RAG-based email system. 
2. **[AML.T0051.000]** They tested prompts on public model APIs to identify effective prompt injections. 
3. **[AML.T0053]** An email containing an adversarial, self-replicating prompt (the "AI worm") was sent to an address used by the target email system; the GenAI assistant automatically ingested the message. 
4. **[AML.T0051.002]** When the worm-laden email was retrieved during another reply-generation task, the prompt injection altered the assistant's behavior. 
5. **[AML.T0061]** The self-replicating portion of the prompt caused generated output to include the malicious prompt itself, enabling further propagation. 
6. **[AML.T0057]** Malicious instructions within the prompt caused generated output to leak sensitive data such as emails, addresses, and phone numbers.

**Recommended ATLAS Mitigations**

- **AML.M0019** - Control Access to AI Models and Data in Production 
- **AML.M0024** - AI Telemetry Logging 
- **AML.M0033** - Input and Output Validation for AI Agent Components 
- **AML.M0020** - Generative AI Guardrails 
- **AML.M0021** - Generative AI Guidelines 
- **AML.M0022** - Generative AI Model Alignment

input: Attack pattern: CAPEC-395 Bypassing Electronic Locks and Access Controls
output:
CAPEC-395: Bypassing Electronic Locks and Access Controls

An attacker exploits security assumptions to bypass electronic locks or other access controls. Although attackers may use different tools, attacks against electronic access controls often follow similar methods. Electronic locks may rely on magnetic strip cards, RFID tags embedded in cards or badges, or more sophisticated protections such as voice-print, thumb-print, or retinal biometrics. Magnetic strip and RFID technologies are the most widespread because they are cost-effective to deploy and easier to integrate with other electronic security measures. These technologies share common weaknesses that an attacker can exploit to gain access to a protected facility.

Abstraction: Standard.

output:
Virat Kohli (Hindi pronunciation:  born 5 November 1988) is an Indian international cricketer and former captain of the Indian national cricket team. He now plays as a right-handed batter for Royal Challengers Bangalore in the IPL and for Delhi in Indian domestic cricket. He is widely recognised as one of the best batsman in cricket history. He is the second most prolific international century batsman in cricket history. The International Cricket Council elected him the male cricketer of the decade despite holding the record for most runs in T20 internationals and the IPL. Kohli has also contributed to a number of India's victories, including the 2011 World Cup and the 2013 Champions Trophy.

Kohli was born and raised in New Delhi, where he attended the West Delhi Cricket Academy and began his junior career with the Delhi Under-15 team. He made his international debut in 2008 and soon established himself as a prominent member of the ODI team, eventually making his Test debut in 2011. For the first time, Kohli topped the ICC ODI batting rankings in 2013. During the 2014 T20 World Cup, he set a competition record for the most runs scored. In 2018, he became the world's top-ranked Test batsman, making him the only Indian cricketer to hold the number one place in all three versions of the game. 
In 2019, he became the first player to score 20,000 international runs in a single decade. Following the T20 World Cup in 2021, Kohli decided to step down as captain of the Indian national team for T20Is, and he stood down as captain of the Test team in early 2022.


He has garnered numerous awards for his achievements on the cricket pitch. He was named the ICC One-Day International Player of the Year in 2012 and has twice won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy, which is awarded to the ICC Cricketer of the Year, in 2017 and 2018. Kohli was the best run scorer in the 2012 Asia Cup, scoring 357 runs. Kohli was also named ICC Test Player of the Year and ICC ODI Player of the Year in 2018, making him the first player to get both honours in the same year. In addition, from 2016 to 2018, he was crowned the Wisden Top Cricketer in the World for three years in a row. Kohli received the Arjuna Award in 2013, the Padma Shri in the sports category in 2017, and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna medal, India's highest sporting honour, in 2018.

instruction: How could a malicious insider abuse T1560, and how would you detect it?
input: Technique in insider context: T1560 - Archive Collected Data
output:
Insider-Threat Analysis - T1560 Archive Collected Data

An adversary may compress and/or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration. Compressing the data can help obfuscate the payload and reduce the amount of traffic sent over the network, while encryption can conceal the content from detection or make the exfiltration less conspicuous during inspection.

Because a trusted insider with legitimate access can perform this activity while blending into normal operations, behavioral baselining is more critical than signature-based detection. Detection should focus on monitoring WinEventLog:Security, WinEventLog:Sysmon, auditd:FILE, and auditd:SYSCALL for anomalous volume, timing, or access that falls outside an individual's role.

Controls to mitigate this technique include enforcing least privilege, separating duties, and applying data-loss-prevention (DLP) measures on sensitive repositories.

instruction: In light of recent incidents where attackers leveraged hidden data exfiltration channels, can you explain the MITRE ATLAS technique AML.T0071 and describe how defenders can mitigate it?
input: ATLAS Technique: AML.T0071 - False RAG Entry Injection
output:
**ATLAS Technique AML.T0071: False RAG Entry Injection**

- **Tactic:** Defense Evasion 
- **Description:** Adversaries can inject fabricated entries into a victim's Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) database. By embedding content that the large language model (LLM) will interpret as a legitimate document within an ingested data source, attackers cause the RAG system to retrieve these false documents. When the LLM processes the retrieved content, it is misled into treating portions of the fabricated entry as genuine RAG output, thereby delivering deceptive information to users.

- **Mitigations:** While no specific ATLAS mitigation is mapped to this technique, general defenses include:
 - Continuous monitoring of model behavior
 - Rigorous input validation before ingestion
 - Restricting access to and visibility of model internals

These controls help reduce the risk that injected false entries will successfully deceive the LLM.

instruction: What are some common software pricing models?
output:
There are many types of software pricing models, but broadly they can be divided into three categories: perpetual, subscription, and consumption.

Perpetual software pricing models, also known as perpetual licensing models, allow the software to be purchased for a one-time fee.  Typically the buyer has nearly unlimited use of the software in perpetuity.  If updates to the software are required, a separate software maintenance package may be purchased.

Subscription software allows unlimited use of the software for a predetermined period, often 1 year or 3 years, for a price.  Updates to the software are often included in the price of the subscription.  At the end of the subscription term, the buyer usually has the option to renew their subscription.

Consumption-based software allows the buyer to pay for their actual usage of the software during a period of time, for example monthly.  In this type of arrangement, the actual usage can vary from period to period, resulting in customer charges that vary as well.  Some customers like knowing that they will only pay for what they use, while other customers dislike the unpredictability of their bills.

instruction: Could you pull up a quick rundown of the key MITRE ATT&CK techniques for the Credential Access tactic, including any detection notes?
input: Tactic: Credential Access
output:
The Credential Access tactic reflects adversaries' efforts to obtain valid credentials during an intrusion. Defenders should focus on detecting activity across the data sources touched by each technique and corroborate multiple signals before generating alerts, as single indicators can often be benign in isolation.

Key techniques and recommended detection sources include:

- **T1556 - Modify Authentication Process**: Monitor AWS CloudTrail, Windows Security event logs, and Sysmon logs for anomalous authentication changes. 
- **T1187 - Forced Authentication**: Inspect network flow data (NSM), Windows Security event logs, and Sysmon logs to identify forced login attempts. 
- **T1517 - Access Notifications**: Use Mobile EDR telemetry and Android MDM logs to spot unauthorized notification access. 
- **T1634 - Credentials from Password Store**: Validate application vetting processes and sensor health checks for suspicious credential extraction. 
- **T1635 - Steal Application Access Token**: Evaluate application vetting results, user interface interactions, and Android logcat output for token theft attempts. 
- **T1110 - Brute Force**: Correlate Windows Security event logs, auditd USER_LOGIN events, and Azure sign-in logs to detect brute-force activity. 
- **T1453 - Abuse Accessibility Features**: Leverage Mobile EDR telemetry to uncover exploitation of accessibility functions. 
- **T1539 - Steal Web Session Cookie**: Analyze Windows Security event logs, Sysmon logs, and auditd SYSCALL events for evidence of session cookie theft.

instruction: Please analyze T1602.002 (Network Device Configuration Dump) from an insider-threat perspective - identify indicators and recommend detection measures.
input: Technique in insider context: T1602.002 - Network Device Configuration Dump
output:
Insider-Threat Analysis - T1602.002 Network Device Configuration Dump

Adversaries can obtain network configuration files to harvest sensitive information about a device and the broader network topology. These configuration files dictate device operation; while the device maintains an in-memory copy during normal operation, it also stores a separate version on non-volatile storage.

Because a trusted insider with legitimate credentials can perform this activity without raising alarms, behavioral baselining is essential - signature-based detection alone is insufficient.

**Detection Recommendations**

- Monitor NSM:Flow, networkdevice:cli, networkdevice:syslog, and snmp:access.
- Generate alerts for anomalous volumes, unusual timing patterns, or access that falls outside an individual's authorized role.

**Control Measures**

- Enforce least privilege and separation of duties.
- Apply DLP controls to protect sensitive configuration repositories.

instruction: Given the reference text about AC Milan, how many FIFA and UEFA trophies have they won?
input:
Associazione Calcio Milan (Italian pronunciation: [assotʃatˈtsjoːne ˈkaltʃo ˈmiːlan]), commonly referred to as AC Milan (Italian pronunciation: [a ˈtʃi ˈmiːlan]) or simply Milan (Italian pronunciation: [miːlan]), is a professional football club in Milan, Italy, founded in 1899. The club has spent its entire history, with the exception of the 1980–81 and 1982–83 seasons, in the top flight of Italian football, known as Serie A since 1929–30.

AC Milan's 18 FIFA and UEFA trophies is the fourth highest out of any club (joint with Boca Juniors[nb 1]), and the most out of any Italian club. Milan has won a joint record three Intercontinental Cups and one FIFA Club World Cup, seven European Cup/Champions League titles (Italian record), the UEFA Super Cup a joint record five times and the Cup Winners' Cup twice. With 19 league titles, Milan is tied as the second most successful club in Serie A with local rivals Inter Milan (also with 19 league titles), behind Juventus (36 league titles). They have also won the Coppa Italia five times, and the Supercoppa Italiana seven.

Milan's home games are played at San Siro, also known as the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza. The stadium, which was built by Milan's second chairman Piero Pirelli in 1926 and is shared since 1947 with city rivals Internazionale, is the largest in Italian football, with a total capacity of 75,923. They have a long-standing rivalry with Inter, with whom they contest the Derby della Madonnina which is one of the most followed derbies in football.

The club is one of the wealthiest in Italian and world football. It was a founding member of the now-defunct G-14 group of Europe's leading football clubs as well as its replacement, the European Club Association.
output: AC Milan has won 18 FIFA and UEFA trophies, which is the fourth most out of any club.

instruction: Provide a concise summary of the impact and recommended countermeasures for CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation - Cross-Site Scripting).
input: Weakness: CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'))
output:
CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-Site Scripting)

**Common consequences**

- **Scope:** Access Control, Confidentiality 
 **Impact:** Bypass Protection Mechanism, Read Application Data. The most frequent exploitation vector involves disclosing private information stored in user cookies - such as session identifiers. A malicious actor typically crafts a payload that is delivered to the victim's browser.

- **Scope:** Integrity, Confidentiality, Availability 
 **Impact:** Execute Unauthorized Code or Commands. In certain scenarios, cross-site scripting can be combined with other vulnerabilities (e.g., "drive-by hacking") to run arbitrary code on a victim's machine.

- **Scope:** Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Access Control 
 **Impact:** Execute Unauthorized Code or Commands, Bypass Protection Mechanism, Read Application Data. Whether the XSS is stored or reflected does not change the fundamental consequence; only the delivery mechanism differs. The payload may arrive at the server through various channels.

**Recommended mitigations (MITRE CWE)**

- Use a vetted library or framework that eliminates this weakness or provides constructs that simplify avoidance [REF-1482]. Examples include Microsoft's Anti-XSS library, the OWASP ESAPI Encoding module, and Apache Wicket.
- Understand the context in which your data will be used and the encoding expected. This is especially critical when transmitting data between components or generating outputs that may contain multiple encodings simultaneously (e.g., web pages or multi-part mail messages). Study all anticipated communication protocols and data representations to determine the required encoding.
- Identify every potential entry point for untrusted input: parameters, arguments, cookies, network reads, environment variables, reverse DNS lookups, query results, request headers, URL components, e-mail, files, filenames, databases, and any external systems that supply data. Remember that such inputs can also be introduced indirectly.
- For any security checks performed on the client side, duplicate them on the server side to avoid CWE-602. Attackers can bypass or remove client-side checks by modifying values after validation or by altering the client entirely; these modified values would then reach the server.

instruction: Given a reference text about the Anglo-Spanish War, tell me what treaty marked the end of the war.
input:
The Anglo-Spanish War (1585–1604) was an intermittent conflict between the Habsburg Kingdom of Spain and the Kingdom of England. It was never formally declared. The war included much English privateering against Spanish ships, and several widely separated battles. It began with England's military expedition in 1585 to what was then the Spanish Netherlands under the command of the Earl of Leicester, in support of the Dutch rebellion against Spanish Habsburg rule.

The English enjoyed a victory at Cádiz in 1587, and repelled the Spanish Armada in 1588, but then suffered heavy setbacks: the English Armada (1589), the Drake–Hawkins expedition (1595), and the Essex–Raleigh expedition (1597). Three further Spanish armadas were sent against England and Ireland in 1596, 1597, and 1601, but these likewise ended in failure for Spain, mainly because of adverse weather.

The war became deadlocked around the turn of the 17th century during campaigns in the Netherlands, France, and Ireland. It was brought to an end with the Treaty of London (1604), negotiated between Philip III of Spain and the new king of England, James I. In the treaty, England and Spain agreed to cease their military interventions in the Spanish Netherlands and Ireland, respectively, and the English ended their high seas privateering.
output: The Treaty of London marked the end of the Anglo-Spanish War.
