instruction: In the following text, identify the key commanders and leaders of the Buddhist Uprising of 1966, extract their roles, and place them in a bulleted list.
input:
The Buddhist Uprising of 1966 (Vietnamese: Nổi dậy Phật giáo 1966), or more widely known in Vietnam as the Crisis in Central Vietnam (Vietnamese: Biến động Miền Trung), was a period of civil and military unrest in South Vietnam, largely focused in the I Corps area in the north of the country in central Vietnam. The area is a heartland of Vietnamese Buddhism, and at the time, activist Buddhist monks and civilians were at the forefront of opposition to a series of military juntas that had been ruling the nation, as well as prominently questioning the escalation of the Vietnam War.

During the rule of the Catholic Ngô Đình Diệm, the discrimination against the majority Buddhist population generated the growth of Buddhist institutions as they sought to participate in national politics and gain better treatment. In 1965, after a series of military coups that followed the fall of the Diệm regime in 1963, Air Marshal Nguyễn Cao Kỳ and General Nguyễn Văn Thiệu finally established a stable junta, holding the positions of Prime Minister and figurehead Chief of State respectively. The Kỳ-Thiệu regime was initially almost a feudal system, being more of an alliance of warlords than a state as each corps commander ruled his area as his own fiefdom, handing some of the taxes they collected over to the government in Saigon and keeping the rest for themselves. During that time, suspicion and tension continued between the Buddhist and Catholic factions in Vietnamese society.

The religious factor combined with a power struggle between Kỳ and General Nguyễn Chánh Thi, the commander of I Corps, a Buddhist local to the region and popular in the area. Thi was a strong-willed officer regarded as a capable commander, and Kỳ saw him as a threat, as did others within the junta. In February 1966, Kỳ attended a summit in Honolulu, where he became convinced that he now had American support to move against Thi, the strongest and most able of the corps commanders. In March 1966, Kỳ fired Thi and ordered him into exile in the United States under the false pretense of medical treatment. This prompted both civilians and some I Corps units to launch widespread civil protests against Kỳ's regime and halt military operations against Viet Cong. Kỳ gambled by allowing Thi to return to I Corps before departing for the US, but the arrival of the general to his native area only fuelled anti-Kỳ sentiment. The Buddhist activists, students and Thi loyalists in the military coalesced into the "Struggle Movement", calling for a return to civilian rule and elections. Meanwhile, Thi stayed in I Corps and did not leave; strikes and protests stopped civilian activity in the area, government radio stations were taken over and used for anti-Kỳ campaigning, and military operations ceased. Riots also spread to the capital Saigon and other cities further south.

At the start of April, Kỳ decided to move. He declared that Da Nang, the main centre in I Corps, was under communist control and publicly vowed to kill the mayor, who had expressed support for the Struggle Movement. Kỳ moved military forces into the city and travelled there to prepare for an assault, but had to withdraw and then start discussions with Buddhist leaders, as it was obvious that he was not strong enough to crush the opposition. In the meantime, he fired Thi's successor Nguyễn Văn Chuân because he wanted a firmer attempt to regain control, and appointed Tôn Thất Đính to replace him. Đính claimed to have calmed the situation, but Kỳ viewed the situation as appeasement, and on May 15, his forces drove off Đính and took over. During the previous month, American forces had also become involved in the stand-off, and the Struggle Movement viewed their participation as biased towards Kỳ, leading to some tense confrontations.

In the second half of May, Kỳ's forces began to force the issue and gradually wore down the Struggle Movement as the rebel I Corps forces were worn down, despite some American objections that his aggressive attacks had the potential to cause too much collateral damage. At one stage, Kỳ's forces ended up in a skirmish with American forces, and later, the Americans were in the middle of a stand-off between the Vietnamese factions regarding a mined bridge. As Kỳ's forces took back Da Nang and Huế in street fighting, Struggle Movement supporters saw American intervention as being pro-Kỳ, and anti-US riots resulted in some American buildings being burnt down. Kỳ's triumph ended the Buddhist movement's influence on politics and he confined their leader Thích Trí Quang to house arrest thereafter, while Thi left for the United States.
output:
-- Nguyễn Cao Kỳ: Air Marshal of South Vietnam leading up to the Buddhist Uprising of 1966. Alongside Nguyễn Văn Thiệu in 1965, he established a stable junta known as the Kỳ-Thiệu regime and held the position of Prime Minister.  This junta felt threatened Commander Thi of the I Corps, forcing his exile as a result.  Thi's exile sparked widespread civil unrest known as the "Struggle Movement".  In the end, Kỳ triumphed over the Buddhist Uprising, ending the Buddhist movement's influence on local politics.
-- Nguyễn Chánh Thi: General of South Vietnam leading up to the Buddhist Uprising of 1966.  The commander of the I Corps, Thi was a a Buddhist local to the region and popular in the area.  He was viewed as a strong-willed officer regarded as a capable commander.  Thi was seen as a threat by the Kỳ-Thiệu junta, and was exiled to the United States as a result by Kỳ.  His exile sparked widespread civil unrest known as the "Struggle Movement".  Thi returned to South Vietnam to help lead the Buddhist Uprising.  In the end, Thi's was defeated, resulting in his return to exile to the United States.

instruction: What would be the ecosystem-wide impact if GHSA-ffhg-7mh4-33c4 (the Go module golang.org/x/crypto) were used as a supply-chain attack vector?
input: Ecosystem: Go  |  Package: golang.org/x/crypto  |  OSV: GHSA-ffhg-7mh4-33c4
output:
The Go package **golang.org/x/crypto** has been identified with a low-severity vulnerability (CVE-2020-9283, GHSA-ffhg-7mh4-33c4) that results from improper verification of cryptographic signatures. The affected version range is **>=0,<0.0.0-20200220183623-bac4c82f6975**.

### Impact
Because *golang.org/x/crypto* is a foundational dependency in the Go ecosystem, any downstream project that pulls an impacted version - whether directly or via transitive dependencies - will inherit this flaw silently. This includes:
- **Direct dependents:** projects that explicitly list *golang.org/x/crypto* in their manifests.
- **Transitive dependents:** projects that acquire the package indirectly through other libraries, which often constitute the majority of exposed consumers.
- **CI/CD and build tooling:** pipelines that install dependencies at build time will also be affected if they resolve an impacted version.
- **Container images:** base images containing the vulnerable package propagate exposure to all layers built atop them.

### Mitigation
- **Registry maintainers** should consider yanking or flagging the affected versions.
- **Project owners** must upgrade to a fixed release. The vulnerability is resolved in **0.0.0-20200220183623-bac4c82f6975**.
- Organizations should enforce dependency scanning within CI pipelines to detect and prevent reintroduction of vulnerable packages.

For further details, see the advisory at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-9283.

instruction: How do I cook the best steak on the bbq?
output:
The best option for cooking a steak on the BBQ is to sear the steaks on the hottest part of the grill for a few minutes on each side, turning only once to form grill marks and then finishing the steaks on the cooler part of the grill for a few more minutes, until the desired doneness is reached. 

Here are the directions for the best results. You’ll want to remove steaks from the refrigerator 20 minutes before grilling and let sit, covered, at room temperature. During this time, preheat your grill on high. 

After 20 minutes, you’ll want to brush the steaks on both sides with oil and season liberally with salt and pepper, or your desired steak seasoning. 

Once the steaks and grill are both ready, you’ll place the steaks on the grill and cook until golden brown and slightly charred, which should take roughly 4 to 5 minutes. Turn the steaks and continue to grill for an additional 4 – 5 minutes for medium-rare, which has an internal temperature of 135 degrees Fahrenheit. For medium, you’ll grill for 5 to 7 minutes or 140 degrees Fahrenheit, or 8 to 10 minutes for medium-well at 150 degrees Fahrenheit. 

At the desired steak temperature, you will remove and transfer the steaks to a cutting board or platter, and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

instruction: What is the YIMBY movement?
output:
YIMBY stands for Yes In My Back Yard. The YIMBY movement is a grassroots response to the phenomenon of NIMBYism, which stands for Not In My Back Yard, and is the name for concentrated local opposition to societally-beneficial resources. For example, NIMBY neighbors might oppose the construction of a new hospital in their neighborhood on the grounds that it will increase local traffic. The whole city will benefit from the new hospital, but the immediate neighbors will oppose it on these grounds regardless of where in the city it is constructed.

The YIMBY movement in the United States is primarily concerned with housing. YIMBY organizations have been formed across the country to support measures that will increase the supply of housing, such as repealing bans on the construction of apartment buildings.

instruction: I'm investigating how deception technology such as honeypots and honeytokens can detect the ATT&CK technique T1684.002 (Email Spoofing).
input: Technique to deceive/detect: T1684.002 - Email Spoofing (Stealth)
output:
Adversaries frequently employ email spoofing (T1684.002) by altering header fields - most notably the FROM header - to impersonate legitimate senders and engage victims under false pretenses. To counter this deception technique, we recommend deploying a layered honey-token strategy that generates high-fidelity alerts with minimal false positives.

**Deception approach**

1. **Decoy assets and honeypots** - Install hosts or services that appear valuable but serve no legitimate purpose. When an adversary interacts with these decoys while attempting to spoof email addresses, the engagement is logged as a potential compromise.
2. **Honeytokens** - Distribute fake credentials, files, or cryptographic keys within the environment. Any use of these tokens signals malicious activity and triggers immediate alerts.
3. **Canary tokens** - Embed tripwires in operational systems that trigger when accessed or referenced by an attacker. These tokens provide early warning of intrusion attempts.

By combining decoy hosts, honeytokens, and canary tokens, organizations can detect and respond to T1684.002 email spoofing with high precision, ensuring that adversaries are identified before they reach genuine targets.

This attack exploits the encoding of URLs and slash characters. An attacker can take advantage of the multiple ways a URL can be encoded to abuse how it is interpreted. URLs may contain special characters that require specific syntax handling. These characters can be represented by a percent sign followed by two digits representing the original character's octet code (%HEX-CODE). For example, the US-ASCII space character is represented as %20; this is known as escaping or percent-encoding. Because servers decode URLs in requests, they may restrict access to certain URL paths by...

- Assume all input is malicious. Create an allowlist, based on the requirements specifications, that defines all valid input to the software system. Do not permit input that does not match the allowlist to enter the system. Test your...
- Be aware of alternative data-encoding and obfuscation techniques, such as IP address encoding.
- When client input is required through web-based forms, avoid using the "GET" method to submit data because it appends form data to the URL, where it can be easily manipulated. Use the "POST method whenever possible.

Both approaches fall under Active Learning.

**Query By Committee (D3A-QBC):** Query by Committee (QBC) draws on ensemble methods. Rather than relying on a single classifier, it considers the decisions of a committee, C=ℎ1,...,ℎc, consisting of classifiers ℎi. Each classifier has the same target classes but uses a different underlying model or a different view of the data.

**Variance Reduction (D3A-VR):** This approach leverages a well-known result from statistical learning that decomposes model error into data noise, model bias, and model variance. Because the noise term depends only on the data and the bias is induced by the choice of model, any reduction in error can come only from reducing the variance term.

instruction: Can you walk me through what CWE-309 is and share the top remediation steps?
input: CWE: CWE-309 — Use of Password System for Primary Authentication
output:
The primary authentication mechanism of a system that relies on passwords is vulnerable to multiple weaknesses, each of which can undermine its effectiveness.

**Consequences if exploited**

- **Scope:** Access Control 
- **Impact:** Attackers can bypass protection mechanisms, gain privileges, or assume the identity of legitimate users. A flaw in password authentication almost always allows an attacker to be authorized as a valid user.

**Mitigations (MITRE CWE)**

1. Store passwords securely so that they cannot be retrieved even if the system is compromised; this protects against insider attacks and mitigates the risk posed by password reuse across other systems. 
2. Employ a zero-knowledge password protocol such as SRP. 
3. Ensure that stored passwords are not reversible. 
4. Implement password aging to force periodic changes.

**OWASP Top 10 2021 mapping**

- A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

Developers should audit code for CWE-309 patterns during design and code-review phases, apply the above mitigations in a defense-in-depth manner, and verify coverage through security testing before deployment.

CWE-1235: Incorrect Use of Autoboxing and Unboxing for Performance Critical Operations

**Scope & Impact** 
This weakness can lead to availability issues by causing a denial-of-service (DoS) through excessive resource consumption - specifically CPU, memory, or other system resources. The performance degradation may reduce overall system responsiveness.

**Recommended Mitigations (MITRE CWE)** 
- Limit the use of boxed primitives to contexts where they are strictly necessary, such as when invoking methods that require typed parameters. 
- Avoid employing boxed primitives in scientific computing or any other performance-critical operations; they should be reserved only for bridging reference types and primitive values. 
- Prior to implementation, thoroughly evaluate the necessity of boxed primitives. 
- Consider alternative data structures - such as SparseArrays or ArrayMap - in place of HashMap when working with large collections that may trigger autoboxing overhead.

instruction: What is the main difference between ORC and Parquet?
output: Both file formats are columnar with similar support for encoding and compression. Their key difference is in how nested data is represented. In Parquet, the nested data is fully shredded into columns with additional metadata to reconstruct the nesting structure. In ORC, nested structures are not decomposed into columns. Rather the nested data value is stored as a regular column value.

instruction: What are the seven main islands of Canary Island as per the passage? Display the results in a comma separated format.
input:
The Canary Islands (/kəˈnɛəri/; Spanish: Canarias, pronounced [kaˈnaɾjas]), also known informally as the Canaries, are a Spanish autonomous community and archipelago in Macaronesia in the Atlantic Ocean. At their closest point to the African mainland, they are 100 kilometres (62 miles) west of Morocco. They are the southernmost of the autonomous communities of Spain. The islands have a population of 2.2 million people and are the most populous special territory of the European Union.

The seven main islands are (from largest to smallest in area) Tenerife, Fuerteventura, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, La Palma, La Gomera, and El Hierro. The archipelago includes many smaller islands and islets, including La Graciosa, Alegranza, Isla de Lobos, Montaña Clara, Roque del Oeste, and Roque del Este. It also includes a number of rocks, including Garachico and Anaga. In ancient times, the island chain was often referred to as "the Fortunate Isles". The Canary Islands are the southernmost region of Spain, and the largest and most populous archipelago of Macaronesia. Because of their location, the Canary Islands have historically been considered a link between the four continents of Africa, North America, South America, and Europe.

In 2019, the Canary Islands had a population of 2,153,389, with a density of 287.39 inhabitants per km2, making it the eighth most populous autonomous community of Spain. The population is mostly concentrated in the two capital islands: around 43% on the island of Tenerife and 40% on the island of Gran Canaria.

The Canary Islands, especially Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura, and Lanzarote, are a major tourist destination, with over 12 million visitors per year. This is due to their beaches, subtropical climate, and important natural attractions, especially Maspalomas in Gran Canaria and Mount Teide (a World Heritage Site) in Tenerife. Mount Teide is the highest peak in Spain and the third tallest volcano in the world, measured from its base on the ocean floor. The islands have warm summers and winters warm enough for the climate to be technically tropical at sea level. The amount of precipitation and the level of maritime moderation vary depending on location and elevation. The archipelago includes green areas as well as desert. The islands' high mountains are ideal for astronomical observation, because they lie above the temperature inversion layer. As a result, the archipelago boasts two professional observatories: the Teide Observatory on Tenerife, and Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma.
output: Tenerife, Fuerteventura, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, La Palma, La Gomera, El Hierro

instruction: Which adversarial techniques were employed in the ATLAS case study "Bypassing Cylance's AI Malware Detection"?
input: ATLAS Case Study: AML.CS0003 — Bypassing Cylance's AI Malware Detection
output:
Skylight Cyber researchers demonstrated a universal bypass string that successfully evaded Cylance's AI-based malware detection when appended to malicious files. The attack, documented on 2019-09-07 against CylancePROTECT and Cylance Smart Antivirus, involved the following ATLAS techniques:

- **AML.T0000** - Search Open Technical Databases (Reconnaissance) 
 Researchers collected publicly available data about Cylance's AI malware detector from sources such as public talks and patent submissions by Cylan. 

- **AML.T0047** - AI-Enabled Product or Service (AI Model Access) 
 They obtained access to Cylance's AI-enabled detection software. 

- **AML.T0063** - Discover AI Model Outputs (Discovery) 
 By enabling verbose logging, they exposed the model's inner workings, including reputation scoring and ensemble behavior. 

- **AML.T0017.000** - Adversarial AI Attacks (Resource Development) 
 Using the reputation scores, researchers reverse-engineered which attributes contributed positively or negatively to a file's reputation. 

- **AML.T0043.003** - Manual Modification (AI Attack Staging) 
 They fused attributes from known benign files with malicious code to craft adversarial malware manually. 

- **AML.T0015** - Evade AI Model (Initial Access, Defense Evasion, Impact) 
 Because a secondary model overrode the primary, the crafted payload bypassed the ML detector entirely.

Mitigations that could have reduced the success of this attack include:

- **AML.M0000** - Limit Public Release of Information 
- **AML.M0024** - AI Telemetry Logging 
- **AML.M0002** - Passive AI Output Obfuscation 
- **AML.M0012** - Encrypt Sensitive Information 
- **AML.M0017** - AI Model Distribution Methods 
- **AML.M0003** - Model Hardening 
- **AML.M0004** - Restrict Number of AI Model Queries 
- **AML.M0006** - Use Ensemble Methods

instruction: What is aliasing?
output: Aliasing is a signal processing phenomenon caused by trying to measure a signal with too low of a sample rate. This means that the time between consecutive measured samples (the sample rate) is too infrequent to properly capture the information of the signal. An example of this is the "carriage wheel" effect, where on film, car tires may appear to go backwards when the car is traveling forwards.

instruction: Could you put together some detection guidance for T1550.001 specifically within our container/Kubernetes environment?
input: Technique: T1550.001 - Application Access Token  | environment: container / Kubernetes
output:
The latest detection engineering guidance focuses on identifying lateral movement attempts that leverage application access tokens within containerized environments such as Kubernetes. The primary tactic under scrutiny is **T1550.001 Application Access Token**.

### Recommended Data Sources
To effectively detect anomalous token usage, collect telemetry from the following platforms:

- **AWS**: CloudTrail logs 
- **Azure**: Sign-in logs 
- **Kubernetes**: API server logs 
- **Microsoft 365**: Unified audit logs 
- **SaaS (Google Workspace)**

### Detection Criteria
Alert on any use of AWS Security Token Service (STS) or Google Cloud Platform IAM APIs that request temporary tokens or federation sessions which deviate from established account behavior. Key indicators include:

- Requests originating from unexpected principals 
- Requests issued in regions not normally used by the account 

### Tuning and Correlation
Because token requests can be legitimate, tune detection rules to align with each platform's normal activity patterns. Correlate signals across multiple data sources before generating an alert to reduce false positives.

By integrating these telemetry streams and applying the outlined criteria, analysts can more accurately surface lateral movement attempts that exploit application access tokens in containerized environments.

instruction: Could you take a look at ATT&CK technique T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation - and break it down in the context of container and Kubernetes security?
input: Technique: T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation  | environment: container / Kubernetes
output:
Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate privileges (T1068). This technique involves taking advantage of programming errors in applications, services, or operating system components - including the kernel - to execute adversary-controlled code. Permission boundaries that normally restrict access to sensitive information or functions can be bypassed through such exploitation.

**Detection guidance for container and Kubernetes environments**

- Windows: monitor `WinEventLog:Security` and `WinEventLog:Sysmon`
- Linux: audit system calls via `auditd:SYSCALL`
- Container runtime: observe `containerd:runtime`
- macOS: watch for relevant events in `macos:endpointsecurity`

**Recommended mitigations**

1. **M1051 - Update Software** 
 Keep all container images, host OSes, and applications up to date with the latest security patches.

2. **M1050 - Exploit Protection** 
 Enable exploit mitigation features such as ASLR, DEP, and stack canaries on hosts and within containers where possible.

3. **M1048 - Application Isolation and Sandboxing** 
 Run containers with the least privilege required, enforce namespaces, cgroups, and SELinux/AppArmor policies to limit the blast radius of a compromised process.

4. **M1019 - Threat Intelligence Program** 
 Integrate threat intelligence feeds that flag known vulnerable components or exploit signatures relevant to containerized workloads.

5. **M1038 - Execution Prevention** 
 Apply execution prevention controls (e.g., Windows Defender Exploit Guard, Linux SELinux policies) to block unauthorized code execution within containers and host systems.

instruction: Give me a supply-chain risk assessment for GHSA-7h4p-27mh-hmrw in django.
input: OSV ID: GHSA-7h4p-27mh-hmrw  |  Package: django (PyPI)
output:
**Supply-Chain Vulnerability - GHSA-7h4p-27mh-hmrw**

* **Package & Ecosystem:** `django` (PyPI) 
* **Alternate Identifiers:** BIT-django-2023-41164, CVE-2023-41164, PYSEC-2023-225 
* **Severity:** LOW 

**Affected Versions** 
- Django 3.2: >= 3.2 and < 3.2.21 
- Django 4.1: >= 4.1 and < 4.1.11 
- Django 4.2: >= 4.2 and < 4.2.5

- 3.2.21, 4.1.11, 4.2.5

---

### Vulnerability Summary
A denial-of-service (DoS) condition exists in `django.utils.encoding.uri_to_iri()` when supplied with inputs containing a very large number of Unicode characters. The flaw is present in the aforementioned Django versions.

### Supply-Chain Impact
Any project that directly or transitively depends on an affected `django` release inherits this vulnerability. Because `django` is widely used as a dependency across the PyPI ecosystem, a single unpatched instance can propagate the risk throughout an entire application graph without downstream consumers' explicit awareness.

### Recommended Action
1. **Pin or upgrade** `django` to a non-affected release (3.2.21, 4.1.11, or 4.2.5). 
2. **Audit** dependency lock files and CI/CD pipelines to ensure the fixed version is resolved both transitively and directly.

For further details, see the advisory at: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-41164

instruction: What is The Masters?
input: The Masters Tournament (usually referred to as simply The Masters, or the U.S. Masters outside North America) is one of the four major championships in professional golf. Scheduled for the first full week of April, the Masters is the first major of the year, and unlike the others, it is always held at the same location, Augusta National Golf Club, a private course in the city of Augusta, Georgia, in the southeastern United States.
output:
The Masters was started by amateur champion Bobby Jones and investment banker Clifford Roberts. After his grand slam in 1930, Jones acquired the former plant nursery and co-designed Augusta National with course architect Alister MacKenzie. First played 89 years ago in 1934, the tournament is an official money event on the PGA Tour, the European Tour, and the Japan Golf Tour. The field of players is smaller than those of the other major championships because it is an invitational event, held by the Augusta National Golf Club.

The tournament has a number of traditions. Since 1949, a green jacket has been awarded to the champion, who must return it to the clubhouse one year after his victory, although it remains his personal property and is stored with other champions' jackets in a specially designated cloakroom. In most instances, only a first-time and currently reigning champion may remove his jacket from the club grounds. A golfer who wins the event multiple times uses the same green jacket awarded upon his initial win (unless they need to be re-fitted with a new jacket). The Champions Dinner, inaugurated by Ben Hogan in 1952, is held on the Tuesday before each tournament, and is open only to past champions and certain board members of the Augusta National Golf Club. Beginning in 1963, legendary golfers, usually past champions, have hit an honorary tee shot on the morning of the first round to commence play. These have included Fred McLeod, Jock Hutchinson, Gene Sarazen, Sam Snead, Byron Nelson, Arnold Palmer, Jack Nicklaus, Gary Player, Lee Elder, and Tom Watson. Since 1960, a semi-social contest at the par-3 course has been played on Wednesday, the day before the first round.

Nicklaus has the most Masters wins, with six between 1963 and 1986. Tiger Woods won five between 1997 and 2019. Palmer won four between 1958 and 1964. Five have won three titles at Augusta: Jimmy Demaret, Sam Snead, Gary Player, Nick Faldo, and Phil Mickelson. Player, from South Africa, was the first non-American player to win the tournament, in 1961; the second was Seve Ballesteros of Spain, the champion in 1980 and 1983.

The Augusta National course first opened 90 years ago in 1933 and has been modified many times by different architects. Among the changes: greens have been reshaped and, on occasion, entirely re-designed, bunkers have been added, water hazards have been extended, new tee boxes have been built, hundreds of trees have been planted, and several mounds have been installed.

instruction: What caused Covid 19?
output: The novel virus was first identified in an outbreak in the Chinese city of Wuhan in December 2019. Attempts to contain it there failed, allowing the virus to spread to other areas of Asia and later worldwide. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern on 30 January 2020, and a pandemic on 11 March 2020. As of 10 March 2023, the pandemic had caused more than 676 million cases and 6.88 million confirmed deaths, making it one of the deadliest in history.

instruction: Explain how an insider might exploit T1052.001 and outline detection methods.
input: Technique in insider context: T1052.001 - Exfiltration over USB
output:
Insider-Threat Analysis: T1052.001 - Exfiltration Over USB

Adversaries may use a USB-connected physical device to exfiltrate data. In scenarios such as an air-gapped network compromise, the exfiltration can occur when a user introduces a USB device into the environment. The device can serve either as the final exfiltration point or as a bridge between otherwise disconnected systems.

Because a trusted insider with legitimate access can carry out this activity while blending in with normal operations, behavioral baselining is more critical than signature-based detection.

**Detection Focus** 
Monitor the following logs and generate alerts on anomalous volume, timing, or access patterns that fall outside an individual's typical role: 
- WinEventLog:Security 
- WinEventLog:Sysmon 
- WinEventLog:System 
- auditd:SYSCALL 

**Controls** 
Implement least privilege and separation of duties. Deploy DLP solutions on sensitive repositories to detect and prevent unauthorized data movement via USB devices.

instruction: Describe the Engage activity System Activity Monitoring and identify the adversary weaknesses it exploits.
input: Engage activity: EAC0003 System Activity Monitoring
output:
Engage activity EAC0003: System Activity Monitoring

System logs can capture logins, user and system events, and other activity. Defenders can use this inherent logging to gather first-hand observations of adversary actions and tools, then send the data to a centralized location for further analysis. Careful planning should guide which logs are collected and at what level: collecting too many logs or setting the logging level too high can overwhelm defenders with excess data. Understanding the adversary's known TTPs can help identify the resources they are likely to touch and, in turn, the logs most likely to capture their activity.

System Activity Monitoring is essential for maintaining situational awareness of adversarial activity, supporting operational safety, and advancing operational goals. Careful pre-operational planning should ensure the engagement environment is properly instrumented and all key network traffic is collected.

Approaches: Collect. Goals served: Expose.

Adversary weaknesses this activity exploits:
- When adversaries interact with network or system resources, they risk triggering tripwires or engaging in easily detectable, anomalous behavior.
- When adversaries interact with the environment or personas, they are vulnerable while collecting, observing, or manipulating system artifacts or information. Manipulated data may cause them to reveal behaviors, use additional or more advanced capabilities against the target, and/or affect their dwell time.

Mapped to 21 ATT&CK techniques, including T1003 OS Credential Dumping; T1036 Masquerading; T1053 Scheduled Task/Job; T1070 Indicator Removal; and T1078 Valid Accounts.

- **T1070.004 - File Deletion**: The malware deletes files to cover its tracks and maintain stealth.
- **T1071.001 - Web Protocols (Command and Control)**: SeaDuke communicates with its command-and-control infrastructure over standard web protocols.
- **T1078 - Valid Accounts**: It uses legitimate credentials to facilitate persistence and stealth operations.

- **T1114.002 - Remote Email Collection**: SeaDuke collects data from remote email accounts, supporting its collection objectives.
- **T1132.001 - Standard Encoding**: It encodes data using standard methods to obfuscate communications with its command-and-control servers.
- **T1546.003 - Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription**: The malware subscribes to WMI events for privilege escalation and persistence.

By mapping SeaDuke's observed behaviors to these techniques, defenders can assess coverage gaps in their detection capabilities and anticipate subsequent malicious activity once the tool is detected within an environment.

instruction: Explain ATT&CK T1598.002 (Spearphishing Attachment) as a social-engineering vector and detail the defenses.
input: Technique: T1598.002 - Spearphishing Attachment | category: social-engineering / credential-harvesting
output:
Social engineering tradecraft - specifically T1598.002 Spearphishing Attachment - is a reconnaissance tactic employed by adversaries to elicit sensitive information that can be leveraged during targeting. By sending spearphishing messages containing malicious attachments, attackers aim to trick targets into disclosing credentials or other actionable data. This form of spearphishing for information often relies on social engineering techniques such as posing as a legitimate source with a plausible reason to collect data (e.g., "Establish Accounts" or "Compromise Accounts") and may involve sending multiple messages.

**Tradecraft context**

Spearphishing Attachment is a core technique in phishing and business email compromise (BEC) operations. Adversaries craft convincing pretexts - impersonating executives, HR personnel, vendors, or financial institutions - to induce victims to click links, open files, or disclose credentials. The low cost of this approach relative to its success rate makes it consistently one of the highest-volume initial-access vectors.

**Defenses**

- Enforce SPF, DKIM, and DMARC on all organisational domains. 
- Deploy a secure email gateway that includes sandboxing, URL rewriting, and impersonation detection. 
- Run regular phishing-simulation exercises and track click-through and reporting rates. 
- Require MFA on all externally accessible services to limit the impact of credential theft. 
- Detect suspicious activity by monitoring application logs and network traffic.

**ATT&CK mitigations**

- M1017: User Training 
- M1054: Software Configuration 

**ATT&CK detection guidance**

Monitor network data for uncommon data flows. Processes that normally do not communicate over the network - or have never been seen communicating before - are suspicious and warrant further investigation.

instruction: What would be the possible impact radius across the crates.io ecosystem if an attacker were to exploit RUSTSEC-2020-0008 in the 'hyper' crate?
input: Ecosystem: crates.io  |  Package: hyper  |  OSV: RUSTSEC-2020-0008
output:
**Blast Radius Analysis - RUSTSEC-2020-0008 (hyper)** 

*Severity:* LOW 
*Affected version range(s):* `>=0.11.0,<0.12.34` 

**Vulnerability Summary** 
The flaw in the Rust crate **hyper** permits request smuggling by allowing a body to be sent with GET requests.

**Supply-Chain Blast Radius** 
The crate is widely used across the crates.io ecosystem, serving as a dependency for many downstream packages and applications. A vulnerability in `hyper` propagates silently through every dependent project that resolves an affected version - including deeply nested transitive dependencies that maintainers may not be aware of.

**Attack Surface Dimensions**

- **Direct dependents:** any project that explicitly lists `hyper` in its manifest within the affected version constraint. 
- **Transitive dependents:** projects that pull `hyper` indirectly via other libraries - often the majority of exposed consumers. 
- **CI/CD and build tooling:** build pipelines that install dependencies at build time are also exposed if they resolve an affected version. 
- **Container images:** base images that bundle affected versions propagate exposure to every image layer built on top.

**Recommended Containment** 
Registry maintainers should consider yanking or flagging affected versions. Dependents should upgrade to a fixed release. The vulnerability is fixed in `0.12.34`. Organizations should enforce dependency scanning in CI to catch re-introductions.

**Advisory:** https://crates.io/crates/hyper

instruction: Could you suggest some ATLAS-aligned countermeasures for the adversarial-ML technique AML.T0063?
input: ATLAS Technique: AML.T0063 - Discover AI Model Outputs
output:
**Mitigation Guidance - AML.T0063: Discover AI Model Outputs**

Adversaries can uncover model outputs - such as class scores - that are unnecessary for system operation and not intended for end-user consumption. These outputs may appear in logs or be embedded within API responses.

**ATLAS-recommended mitigations**

- **AML.M0002 Passive AI Output Obfuscation** - Obfuscate model outputs to impede adversaries from harvesting sensitive information.
- **AML.M0012 Encrypt Sensitive Information** - Encrypt model outputs to protect the AI system's internal workings and operations from discovery.
- **AML.M0017 AI Model Distribution Methods** - Avoid deploying models to edge devices, thereby limiting an attacker's ability to capture output data.
- **AML.M0019 Control Access to AI Models and Data in Production** - Restrict production-environment access to the model so adversaries cannot infer details from outputs.

Defenders should apply these controls in layers and maintain continuous monitoring. Adversarial-ML attacks often succeed when prevention is incomplete, making detection capabilities essential even with mitigations in place.

instruction: Devise an active-defense or deception measure specifically aimed at intercepting adversary use of T1071.003 (mail protocols).
input: Technique to deceive/detect: T1071.003 - Mail Protocols (Command and Control)
output:
Adversaries often employ application-layer protocols tied to electronic mail delivery (MITRE ATT&CK technique T1071.003) to conceal command and control traffic by blending it with legitimate email flows. By embedding commands and their results within such protocol traffic, they can evade detection and network filtering.

To counter this deception strategy, organizations should deploy a layered honey-token approach that creates high-fidelity alerts while maintaining near-zero false positives:

- **Honeytokens**: Deploy fake credentials, files, or cryptographic keys. Any use of these tokens signals a compromise.
- **Honeypot/Decoy Hosts**: Place decoy servers and assets with no legitimate business purpose to attract adversary interaction and capture their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
- **Canary Tokens**: Embed tripwires within real production systems. When triggered, they provide early warning of malicious activity.

By combining these measures, an organization can detect the use of mail-based command and control channels with high precision while minimizing alert fatigue.

instruction: Could you build an incident-response plan per NIST SP 800-61 for activity using ATT&CK T1543.002 (Systemd Service)?

**Incident Response Plan (NIST SP 800-61) - T1543.002 Systemd Service**

**Detection & Analysis** 
Validate the alert by inspecting auditd:SYSCALL and linux:osquery logs for creation or modification of `.service` unit files in system/user-level directories, coupled with execution of `systemctl`, `service`, or dynamically created drop-ins via systemd generators. Confirm persistence by analyzing the `ExecStart` path, file entropy, and symlink usage - particularly when the executable is located in a non-standard directory or exhibits high entropy indicative of packed code.

Scope the incident to identify affected hosts and accounts, ensuring that the activity represents a legitimate Systemd service installation (persistence or privilege escalation) rather than a benign false positive.

**Containment, Eradication & Recovery** 
1. Isolate compromised assets; disable or rotate implicated user accounts. 
2. Remove all foothold artifacts and restore affected systems from known-good backups or configuration baselines. 
3. Implement preventive controls to block recurrence: 
 * M1018 - User Account Management 
 * M1022 - Restrict File and Directory Permissions 
 * M1026 - Privileged Account Management 
 * M1033 - Limit Software Installation 

**Post-Incident Activity** 
Collect forensic evidence, document the incident timeline, and incorporate lessons learned into the organization's preparation phase by updating detections, hardening measures, and playbooks.

instruction: How wide could the blast radius be across the crates.io ecosystem if an attacker exploits RUSTSEC-2025-0004 in "openssl"?
input: Ecosystem: crates.io  |  Package: openssl  |  OSV: RUSTSEC-2025-0004
output:
The Rust package `openssl` is affected by the vulnerability identified as **RUSTSEC-2025-0004** (ssl::select_next_proto use after free). The vulnerable versions span the range **>=0.0.0-0,<0.10.70**.

### Supply-Chain Blast Radius
Any crate that pulls in `openssl` - whether directly or indirectly - may silently inherit this flaw. Because `openssl` is a common dependency across many downstream packages and applications, the impact extends to deeply nested transitive dependencies that maintainers may not be aware of.

### Attack Surface Dimensions
- **Direct dependents**: Projects that explicitly list `openssl` in their manifest with an affected version constraint.
- **Transitive dependents**: Projects that acquire `openssl` indirectly via other libraries - often the majority of exposed consumers.
- **CI/CD and build tooling**: Build pipelines that install dependencies at build time are also vulnerable if they resolve an affected version.
- **Container images**: Base images bundling affected versions propagate exposure to every image layer built on top.

### Recommended Containment
Registry maintainers should consider yanking or flagging the affected versions. Dependents should upgrade to a fixed release (`0.10.70`). Organizations should enforce dependency scanning in CI to catch re-introductions.

**Advisory link:** https://crates.io/crates/openssl

instruction: In the Engage activity framework, what does Information Manipulation involve, and which adversary weaknesses does it exploit?
input: Engage activity: EAC0015 Information Manipulation
output:
Engage activity EAC0015: Information Manipulation

Information Manipulation supports the engagement narrative and directly impacts adversary activities. Revealed facts and fictions can adjust the adversary's trust in the environment, while concealed facts and fictions can affect the adversary's sense of uncertainty.

Revealed facts may include OS type and version, geographic location, hardware type and version, accounts, and credentials. Revealed fictions may include the content of decoy files, emails, and messages. Adversaries may or may not believe revealed facts or fictions. If they do, these disclosures may lend credibility to the environment or encourage a specific action. If they are suspicious of or do not believe them, the disclosures may erode trust in the environment or discourage a specific action. Revealed facts and fictions can therefore be used to adjust adversary trust in ways that support operational objectives.

Concealed facts may include virtualized systems disguised as physical systems, monitoring software, or collection efforts. Concealed fictions may include an encrypted, interestingly named decoy file or a partially deleted email thread referencing high-value but decoy assets. Adversaries may or may not discover concealed facts and fictions. If they do, discovery may increase environmental ambiguity and affect their sense of uncertainty. Concealed facts and fictions can therefore be used to adjust ambiguity and uncertainty in ways that support operational objectives.

Approaches: Reassure, Motivate. Goals served: Elicit.

Adversary weaknesses this activity exploits:
- When adversaries discover a diverse set of accessible resources and decoy artifacts on the target, they are vulnerable to revealing their targeting preferences and capabilities.
- When adversaries interact with the environment or personas, they are vulnerable while collecting, observing, or manipulating system artifacts or information. Manipulated data may cause them to reveal behaviors, use additional or more advanced capabilities against the target, and/or affect their dwell time.

Mapped to 54 ATT&CK techniques, for example: T1001 Data Obfuscation; T1005 Data from Local System; T1007 System Service Discovery; T1010 Application Window Discovery; T1011 Exfiltration Over Other Network Medium.

instruction: Can you summarize for me in no more than three paragraphs the book, "The Little Engine That Could", by Watty Piper?
input: The Little Engine That Could is an American folktale (existing in the form of several illustrated children's books and films) that became widely known in the United States after publication in 1930 by Platt & Munk. The story is used to teach children the value of optimism and hard work. Based on a 2007 online poll, the National Education Association listed the book as one of its "Teachers' Top 100 Books for Children"
output:
The Little Engine That Could is a children's book written in 1930 by Watty Piper.  The main purpose of the book is to help bring out in children a positive, "can-do attitude."  The key phrase in the book is, "I think I can." 

The main character is the "Little Engine".  The Little Engine is an undersized locomotive that is called upon to pull rail cars full of good things for the boys and girls that live on the other side of the mountain.  Several other locomotives, appearing newer, stronger or more mature than the Little Engine all make excuses for why they will not help take the train cars over the mountain.

The Little Engine gladly takes on the task when called upon.  When starting to pull the heavy rail cars, The Little Engine strains with all its might and begins to say, "I think I can, I think I can, I think I can."  When climbing the mountain, it doesn't look like the Little Engine has the power to get over the peak.  The Little Engine puffs, "I think I can, I think I can, I think I can."  Finally The Little Engine reaches the top, comes over the crest and on the way down says, "I though I could, I thought I could, I thought I could."

instruction: What techniques do honeypots and honeytokens employ to detect ATT&CK T1588.002 (Tool)?
input: Technique to deceive/detect: T1588.002 - Tool (Resource Development)
output:
Adversaries often acquire or develop software tools - whether open-source, proprietary, free, or commercial - that can be leveraged during a targeting phase (MITRE ATT&CK T1588.002). Although such tools are not inherently malicious, they may be repurposed for illicit use, as exemplified by utilities like PsExec.

A robust deception strategy mitigates this risk by deploying decoy assets and honeytokens that serve no legitimate purpose. Interaction with these artifacts during an adversary's resource-development activities triggers high-fidelity alerts while maintaining near-zero false positives. Key components of this approach include:

- **Honeytokens**: fabricated credentials, files, or cryptographic keys whose usage signals a compromise.
- **Honeypot/Decoy Hosts**: engineered systems designed to attract adversarial interaction and capture their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
- **Canary Tokens**: embedded tripwires within operational environments that provide early warning when triggered.

By integrating these elements into the security posture, organizations can effectively detect and respond to tool acquisition attempts by malicious actors.

instruction: Hey, could you tell me which OWASP Top 10 2021 category includes CWE-652 (Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions - XQuery Injection) and what the recommended fix is?
input: Weakness: CWE-652 (Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions ('XQuery Injection'))
output:
CWE-652 - Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions (XQuery Injection) maps directly to OWASP Top 10 2021 category A03:2021. The core impact is that an attacker can dictate the data selected from an XML database, enabling manipulation of application flow, alteration of logic, retrieval of unauthorized information, or bypassing critical controls such as authentication.

**Mitigation Recommendations (MITRE CWE guidance)** 
- Employ parameterized queries to enforce a strict separation between the data plane and the control plane. 
- Rigorously validate user input: reject disallowed data, filter where appropriate, and escape content that will be embedded in XQL statements to ensure it is safe for that context.

Effectively addressing CWE-652 requires implementing these mitigations and verifying coverage of all scenarios outlined in OWASP A03:2021. Validation should combine automated SAST/DAST tooling with thorough manual code review to confirm the vulnerability has been fully remediated.

**Campaign Overview - C0035**

*Active Period:* 2022-10-01 - 2024-01-01

Volt Typhoon leveraged the KV Botnet to obscure its communications with victims across several critical infrastructure sectors, notably energy and telecommunications. The botnet's primary vector was the exploitation of "end-of-life" small office/home office (SOHO) devices from vendors such as Cisco, NETGEAR, and DrayTek. Victims included entities located within the United States territory of Guam. instruction: Extract the areas of science using differential equations in this text in an alphabetically ordered list.
input:
A differential equation is a mathematical equation for an unknown function of one or several variables that relates the values of the function itself and its derivatives of various orders. Differential equations play a prominent role in engineering, physics, economics, biology, and other disciplines.

Differential equations arise in many areas of science and technology, specifically whenever a deterministic relation involving some continuously varying quantities (modelled by functions) and their rates of change in space or time (expressed as derivatives) is known or postulated. This is illustrated in classical mechanics, where the motion of a body is described by its position and velocity as the time value varies. Newton's laws allow one (given the position, velocity, acceleration and various forces acting on the body) to express these variables dynamically as a differential equation for the unknown position of the body as a function of time. In some cases, this differential equation (called an equation of motion) may be solved explicitly.
output:
Here is a list of alphabetically sorted applications of differential equations:
- Biology
- Economics
- Engineering
- Physics

instruction: Can you list the consequences and suggest mitigations for CWE-401 (Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime)?
input: Weakness: CWE-401 (Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime)
output:
CWE-401 - Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

**Common Consequences**

*Scope: Availability.* 
Impact includes denial-of-service conditions such as crash, exit or restart; system instability; and resource consumption attacks targeting CPU or memory. While most memory leaks simply degrade product reliability, an attacker who can deliberately trigger a leak may initiate a DoS attack by exhausting critical resources.

*Scope: Other.* 
Impact also encompasses reduced performance due to inefficient memory usage.

**Recommended Mitigations (MITRE CWE)**

1. Select a language or tool that offers automatic memory management, or otherwise reduces the risk of manual errors. For example:
 * In Linux, glibc provides protection against freeing invalid pointers.
 * When using Xcode for OS X or iOS development, enable Automatic Reference Counting (ARC) [REF-391].
 * In C++, employ smart pointers to consistently manage memory.

2. Use an abstraction library to encapsulate risky APIs; this can mitigate but does not eliminate the risk entirely.

3. Consider integrating the Boehm-Demers-Weiser garbage collector (bdwgc), which helps prevent leaks by automatically reclaiming unused memory.

instruction: Using examples taken from the text give me a rundown of the primary environments found in Yellowstone National Park.
input:
Yellowstone National Park is an American national park located in the western United States, largely in the northwest corner of Wyoming and extending into Montana and Idaho. It was established by the 42nd U.S. Congress with the Yellowstone National Park Protection Act and signed into law by President Ulysses S. Grant on March 1, 1872. Yellowstone was the first national park in the U.S. and is also widely held to be the first national park in the world. The park is known for its wildlife and its many geothermal features, especially the Old Faithful geyser, one of its most popular. While it represents many types of biomes, the subalpine forest is the most abundant. It is part of the South Central Rockies forests ecoregion.

While Native Americans have lived in the Yellowstone region for at least 11,000 years, aside from visits by mountain men during the early-to-mid-19th century, organized exploration did not begin until the late 1860s. Management and control of the park originally fell under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Department of the Interior, the first Secretary of the Interior to supervise the park being Columbus Delano. However, the U.S. Army was eventually commissioned to oversee the management of Yellowstone for 30 years between 1886 and 1916. In 1917, administration of the park was transferred to the National Park Service, which had been created the previous year. Hundreds of structures have been built and are protected for their architectural and historical significance, and researchers have examined more than a thousand archaeological sites.

Yellowstone National Park spans an area of 3,468.4 sq mi (8,983 km2), comprising lakes, canyons, rivers, and mountain ranges. Yellowstone Lake is one of the largest high-elevation lakes in North America and is centered over the Yellowstone Caldera, the largest super volcano on the continent. The caldera is considered a dormant volcano. It has erupted with tremendous force several times in the last two million years. Well over half of the world's geysers and hydrothermal features are in Yellowstone, fueled by this ongoing volcanism. Lava flows and rocks from volcanic eruptions cover most of the land area of Yellowstone. The park is the centerpiece of the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem, the largest remaining nearly-intact ecosystem in the Earth's northern temperate zone. In 1978, Yellowstone was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Hundreds of species of mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, and amphibians have been documented, including several that are either endangered or threatened. The vast forests and grasslands also include unique species of plants. Yellowstone Park is the largest, and most famous megafauna location in the contiguous United States. Grizzly bears, cougars, wolves, and free-ranging herds of bison and elk live in this park. The Yellowstone Park bison herd is the oldest and largest public bison herd in the United States. Forest fires occur in the park each year; in the large forest fires of 1988, nearly one-third of the park was burnt. Yellowstone has numerous recreational opportunities, including hiking, camping, boating, fishing, and sightseeing. Paved roads provide close access to the major geothermal areas as well as some of the lakes and waterfalls. During the winter, visitors often access the park by way of guided tours that use either snow coaches or snowmobiles.
output: Generally considered to be the first national park in the world, Yellowstone National Park is significant in size, covering parts of Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho, and acts as the largest remaining nearly-intact ecosystems.  The park is able to support many types of wildlife including Grizzly bears, cougars, wolves, mountain goats, free-ranging herds of bison and elk, as well as many types of birds and fish, because of the diversity of habitats.  Forests and grasslands dominate some areas of the park, while others offer the completely different experience of mountain ranges, lakes, and rolling prairies.  Some of the park's most unique features are the geysers and hydrothermal features.  In fact, Yellowstone is home to over half of the world's features like these.  This is due to the entire park being centered over the Yellowstone Caldera, the largest super volcano on the continent.

instruction: Could you explain what the Engage activity Email Manipulation involves and which adversary weaknesses it exploits?
input: Engage activity: EAC0009 Email Manipulation
output:
Engage activity EAC0009: Email Manipulation

Email Manipulation encompasses methods for affecting email flows in an environment, including which mail appliances process them, where messages are forwarded, and what appears in an inbox. A common use is to introduce malware into the engagement environment. For example, suspicious emails may be removed from a production mailbox and placed in an engagement-environment inbox so that suspicious attachments or links can be detonated there. Alternatively, emails collected over a long period from a legitimate inbox outside the environment may be moved into it, creating a more lived-in mailbox that helps reassure the adversary of the environment's legitimacy.

Approaches: Direct, Reassure. Goals served: Affect, Elicit.

Adversary weaknesses this activity exploits:
- When adversaries interact with the environment or personas, they are vulnerable while collecting, observing, or manipulating system artifacts or information. Manipulated data may cause them to reveal behaviors, use additional or more advanced capabilities against the target, and/or affect their dwell time.
- When adversaries interact with the environment or personas, they are vulnerable to collecting or otherwise interacting with manipulated or decoy data. This data may increase their tolerance for imperfections in the environment and improve the overall believability of the ruse.

Mapped to 3 ATT&CK techniques, for example: T1114 Email Collection; T1119 Automated Collection; T1566 Phishing.

The group is composed of nine members: Nayeon, Jeongyeon, Momo, Sana, Jihyo, Mina, Dahyun, Chaeyoung, and Tzuyu. Twice was formed under the television program Sixteen (2015) and debuted on October 20, 2015, with the extended play (EP) The Story Begins.

Their next single, "TT", from their third EP Twicecoaster: Lane 1, topped the Gaon charts for four consecutive weeks. The EP was the highest selling Korean girl group album of 2016. As of December 2020, the group has sold over 15 million albums cumulatively in South Korea and Japan.

The group debuted in Japan on June 28, 2017, under Warner Music Japan, with the release of a compilation album titled #Twice. The album charted at number 2 on the Oricon Albums Chart with the highest first-week album sales by a K-pop artist in Japan in two years. It was followed by the release of Twice's first original Japanese maxi single titled "One More Time" in October. Twice became the first Korean girl group to earn a platinum certification from the Recording Industry Association of Japan (RIAJ) for both an album and CD single in the same year. With the release of their single "Feel Special" in 2019, Twice became the third female Korean act to chart into the Canadian Hot 100. Their first official English-language single, "The Feels", became their first song to enter the US Billboard Hot 100 and the UK Singles Chart, peaking at the 83rd and 80th positions of the charts, respectively. (2018)—became dance crazes and viral memes imitated by many celebrities.

instruction: Who was Margaret Thatcher?
input: Margaret Hilda Thatcher, Baroness Thatcher, LG, OM, DStJ, PC, FRS, HonFRSC (née Roberts; 13 October 1925 – 8 April 2013), was a British politician and stateswoman who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1979 to 1990 and Leader of the Conservative Party from 1975 to 1990. She was the first female British prime minister and the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century. As prime minister, she implemented economic policies that became known as Thatcherism. A Soviet journalist dubbed her the "Iron Lady", a nickname that became associated with her uncompromising politics and leadership style.
output: Margaret Thatcher was the first woman to be elected prime minister of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, serving in this role from her first election victory in 1979 until she was forced out of office by members of her own party in 1990. During this time she transformed the economic situation in the United Kingdom by introducing economic policies intended to reverse high inflation and weak growth. By constraining the power of trades unions and overseeing extensive deregulation and privatisation, Thatcher helped to create a period of extended growth and economic success. Together with Ronald Reagan, she was also instrumental in recognising and supporting the opportunity to end communist rule in the Soviet Union, where she was dubbed the 'Iron Lady', through her friendship with the Russian leader, Mikhail Gorbachev. Her legacy was to end the so-called 'post-war consensus' in the UK (characterised by high taxes, regulation and nationalisation) and to replace it with policies that encouraged free-enterprise and personal responsibility while acknowledging the importance of the welfare state, provided it was administered responsibly. Although disliked by many on the left for the way that she challenged excessive union power, she is generally acknowledged as the most important British politician of the late twentieth century.

instruction: Create an active-defense or deception measure specifically designed to detect and intercept activity labeled T0807 (Command-Line Interface).

To detect such activity, a deception strategy can be implemented by deploying decoy assets and honeytokens that serve no legitimate purpose. When an adversary attempts to use the CLI against these decoys - effectively executing T0807 (Command-Line Interface) - the system generates a high-fidelity alert with virtually zero false positives.

* **Honeytokens** - fabricated credentials, files, or keys that trigger a compromise signal when accessed.
* **Honeypot/decoy hosts** - engineered to attract interaction and capture the adversary's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
* **Canary tokens** - embedded tripwires within real systems that provide early warning of unauthorized activity.

By integrating these elements, defenders can effectively surface CLI-based attacks while minimizing noise in their alerting pipeline.

instruction: What are financial instruments?
output:
Financial instruments are monetary contracts between parties. They can be created, traded, modified and settled. They can be cash (currency), evidence of an ownership interest in an entity or a contractual right to receive or deliver in the form of currency (forex); debt (bonds, loans); equity (shares); or derivatives (options, futures, forwards).

International Accounting Standards IAS 32 and 39 define a financial instrument as "any contract that gives rise to a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability or equity instrument of another entity".

Financial instruments may be categorized by "asset class" depending on whether they are equity-based (reflecting ownership of the issuing entity) or debt-based (reflecting a loan the investor has made to the issuing entity). If the instrument is debt it can be further categorized into short-term (less than one year) or long-term. Foreign exchange instruments and transactions are neither debt- nor equity-based and belong in their own category.

instruction: What is a quantum computer?
output:
A quantum computer is a computer that exploits quantum mechanical phenomena. At small scales, physical matter exhibits properties of both particles and waves, and quantum computing leverages this behavior using specialized hardware. Classical physics cannot explain the operation of these quantum devices, and a scalable quantum computer could perform some calculations exponentially faster than any modern "classical" computer. In particular, a large-scale quantum computer could break widely used encryption schemes and aid physicists in performing physical simulations; however, the current state of the art is still largely experimental and impractical.

The basic unit of information in quantum computing is the qubit, similar to the bit in traditional digital electronics. Unlike a classical bit, a qubit can exist in a superposition of its two "basis" states, which loosely means that it is in both states simultaneously. When measuring a qubit, the result is a probabilistic output of a classical bit. If a quantum computer manipulates the qubit in a particular way, wave interference effects can amplify the desired measurement results. The design of quantum algorithms involves creating procedures that allow a quantum computer to perform calculations efficiently.

Physically engineering high-quality qubits has proven challenging. If a physical qubit is not sufficiently isolated from its environment, it suffers from quantum decoherence, introducing noise into calculations. National governments have invested heavily in experimental research that aims to develop scalable qubits with longer coherence times and lower error rates. Two of the most promising technologies are superconductors (which isolate an electrical current by eliminating electrical resistance) and ion traps (which confine a single atomic particle using electromagnetic fields).

Any computational problem that can be solved by a classical computer can also be solved by a quantum computer. Conversely, any problem that can be solved by a quantum computer can also be solved by a classical computer, at least in principle given enough time. In other words, quantum computers obey the Church–Turing thesis. This means that while quantum computers provide no additional advantages over classical computers in terms of computability, quantum algorithms for certain problems have significantly lower time complexities than corresponding known classical algorithms. Notably, quantum computers are believed to be able to solve certain problems quickly that no classical computer could solve in any feasible amount of time—a feat known as "quantum supremacy." The study of the computational complexity of problems with respect to quantum computers is known as quantum complexity theory.

instruction: Considering the ATLAS taxonomy for adversarial machine learning, could you list the techniques that fall under the Exfiltration tactic?
input: ATLAS Tactic: AML.TA0010 — Exfiltration
output:
The adversary's objective under the MITRE ATLAS tactic **AML.TA0010 - Exfiltration** is to obtain AI artifacts or other information about an AI system. The techniques employed include:

- **AML.T0077 - LLM Response Rendering:** The attacker may prompt a large language model (LLM) to produce responses that reveal private information hidden from the user.
- **AML.T0024.001 - Invert AI Model:** By exploiting confidence scores available through inference, the adversary can reconstruct training data for an AI model.
- **AML.T0056 - Extract LLM System Prompt:** Adversaries may use prompt injection to extract a large language model's system prompt.
- **AML.T0057 - LLM Data Leakage:** The attacker may craft prompts that induce the LLM to leak sensitive information.
- **AML.T0024.000 - Infer Training Data Membership:** The adversary can infer whether a specific data sample or global characteristics of the training set are present, revealing membership details.
- **AML.T0024.002 - Extract AI Model:** Adversaries may extract a functional copy of a private model.
- **AML.T0024 - Exfiltration via AI Inference API:** The attacker can exfiltrate private information through access to an AI Model Inference API.
- **AML.T0025 - Exfiltration via Cyber Means:** Traditional cyber methods are used to exfiltrate AI artifacts or other relevant information.
- **AML.T0086 - Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation:** AI agent tools capable of performing write operations may be invoked by the adversary to transfer data to an external destination.

instruction: Given the reference text below, who sang "It's a Great Day to Be Alive"?
input:
"It's a Great Day to Be Alive" is a song written by Darrell Scott. It was originally recorded by American country music artist Jon Randall, of whose version was to have been included on an album titled Great Day to Be Alive, which would have been released in the late 1990s via BNA Records. Scott released his own version of his song on his 1997 album Aloha from Nashville.

The song was also recorded by The Sky Kings, an American country-rock supergroup consisting of Bill Lloyd (Foster & Lloyd), Rusty Young (Poco), and John Cowan (New Grass Revival) around 1995/1996. Their version sat unreleased until Rhino Handmade released the compilation "From Out Of The Blue" in 2000.

The song was later covered more famously by American country music artist Travis Tritt. It was released in December 2000 as the second single from his album Down the Road I Go. It peaked at number 2 on the U.S. Billboard Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart and at number 33 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart.

It was subsequently covered by Pat Green and Cory Morrow on their March 2001 album Songs We Wish We'd Written and by Niko Moon for his 2021 album Good Time.
output: "It's a Great Day to Be Alive" is a song written by Darrell Scott which was released in December 2000.

instruction: How do you make pizza?
output:
Pizza comes in many styles. I make Neapolitan pizza, which generally requires a high hydration dough and a very high oven temperatures. The dough is made with four cups of flour, three tablespoons olive oil, a cup and a half of water, one package of yeast, a tablespoon of sugar, and a teaspoon and a half of salt. I typically activate the yeast in lukewarm water and sugar first, then mix all the ingredients in a stand mixer with a dough attachment. I'll add additional water until the dough is very wet, let it rise once in the mixing bowl, then turn the dough out on a surface coated generously with flour. Then I quarter the dough, fold a few times, and let rise again. 

Forming the pies is the tricky part. I've found pushing the dough into a rough circle with my fingers as a first step works well, but he dough will tend to snap back. I'll pick up the small dough circle and stretch it out on top of my fists to start to break the gluten and form a larger pie with a thinner base. I use an Ooni oven pre-heated on high, but turn the heat down when I'm ready to put the pizza in. The peel needs to be generously coated with flour to get a good launch into the oven. After a few seconds, the dough on the bottom will cook enough that manipulating the pizza becomes much easier. I keep the toppings simple, mozzarella (low moisture), tomato sauce, basil. 

Enjoy!

instruction: Can you explain what CWE-798 is and list the ways we can mitigate it?
input: CWE: CWE-798 — Use of Hard-coded Credentials
output:
**CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials**

The vulnerability manifests in two primary forms:

1. **Inbound** - The product embeds an authentication routine that validates user input against a hard-coded credential set. A default administrative account is created with a simple, immutable password that is identical across all installations. System administrators cannot disable or alter this credential without manually modifying the binary or applying a patch, and detection of its presence can be difficult.

2. **Outbound** - The product establishes connections to external systems or components using hard-coded credentials. This pattern typically occurs in front-end systems that authenticate with back-end services.

---

### Potential Impact

- **Scope: Access Control / Bypass Protection Mechanism** 
 An attacker who discovers the hard-coded password can almost certainly gain access to the associated account, thereby compromising any functionality tied to it.

- **Scope: Integrity, Confidentiality, Availability, Access Control, Other** 
 Exploitation may allow an adversary to read application data, elevate privileges or impersonate legitimate users, execute unauthorized code or commands, and generally expose resources or functionality to unintended actors. In some cases this could even enable arbitrary code execution if the password is used in a privileged context.

---

### Mitigation Guidance (MITRE CWE)

- **Outbound Authentication** - Store credentials, keys, and other secrets outside of source code in a strongly protected, encrypted configuration file or database that is inaccessible to all external parties, including local users. Protect the encryption key appropriately (CWE-320). If encryption cannot be employed, enforce restrictive permissions on the credential store.

- **Inbound Authentication** - Replace hard-coded default usernames and passwords with a "first-login" mode that forces the user to set a unique, strong password or key upon initial setup.

- **When Hard-coded Credentials Are Unavoidable** - Implement access control checks to limit which entities can invoke features requiring those credentials. For example, restrict such functionality to local console use rather than exposing it over the network.

- **Password Handling** - Store only strong one-way hashes of passwords in configuration files or databases with proper access controls. Even if an attacker obtains the hash file, they must still crack the password. During authentication, hash the supplied password and compare it against the stored hash.

---

### OWASP Top 10 Mapping

- **A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures** 

Developers should audit code for CWE-798 patterns during design and code-review phases, apply the above mitigations in a defense-in-depth manner, and validate coverage through security testing before deployment.

instruction: Could you explain the MITRE Engage activity 'Burn-In' and when an analyst should use it?
input: Engage activity: EAC0008 Burn-In
output:
Engage activity EAC0008: Burn-In

Burn-In involves exercising a system to create desirable artifacts, such as web browsing history, file system usage, or evidence of user applications running. Sometimes, this can be achieved simply by allowing a system or application to run for an extended period. In other cases, the defender actively engages with the environment to generate artifacts - for example, by logging into a decoy account or visiting a decoy website to create session cookies and browser history. These tasks can be performed manually or with automated tooling.

Burn-In should take place pre-operation and continue as appropriate during the operation. The resulting artifacts can reassure the adversary that the environment is legitimate by making it more closely resemble a real, lived-in system or network.

Approach: Reassure. Goal served: Elicit.

Adversary weaknesses exploited by this activity:
- When adversaries interact with the environment or personas, they may collect or otherwise interact with manipulated or decoy data. This can increase their tolerance for imperfections in the environment and improve the overall believability of the ruse.
- When adversaries discover a diverse set of accessible resources and decoy artifacts on the target, they may reveal their targeting preferences and capabilities.

Mapped to 13 ATT&CK techniques, including T1005 Data from Local System; T1012 Query Registry; T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery; T1049 System Network Connections Discovery; and T1057 Process Discovery.

instruction: What is 'karma' according to Buddhism?
output:
Karma is a central and fundamental aspect of Buddhist doctrine common to all traditions of Buddhism. The Buddhist concept of Karma is a natural process that operates with all our volitional actions and which does not need an external agency or power that sits in judgement.

Karma in Buddhism should not be considered as moral justice, or a method of reward and punishment, that needs an external body or authority to decide whom or what should be punished and rewarded. It is believed that Gautama Buddha attained complete insight into how the process of Karma works during the night of his full enlightenment when, through the divine eye (dibbacakku), Buddha saw how other beings die and are reborn in happy and unhappy states according to their Karma.

According to the Cula-kammavibhanga sutta of the Majima Nikava (collection of the middle length discourses of the Buddha), a young brahmin by the name of Subha had approached the Buddha and inquired as to why there was so much inequality among human beings in terms of being short-lived or long-lived, sickly or healthy, ugly or beautiful, powerful or powerless, poor or rich, low-born or high-born, ignorant or intelligent, etc. Buddha had then explained that:
"all living beings are the owners of their actions, heirs to their actions, they originate from their actions, they are related through their actions, they have their actions as their refuge and that it is action or Karma that distinguishes beings as inferior and superior

The word Karma in Pali, and karma in Sanskrit, means action but encompasses only actions that are intentional, volitional and willful and which will lead to consequences sooner or later. The mind (citta) by itself cannot perform or direct any mental, verbal or physical action and it is the intention, will, mental effort or volition (cetana) that directs any mental, verbal or physical action.

Thus the Buddha declared:
"Cetanaham bhikkhave kammam vadami
Cetayitva kammam karoti, kayena, vacaya, manasa"

"It is volition that I call Karma, by volition one performs Karma through body, word or mind."

Adversaries can automate the gathering of industrial environment data by employing tools or scripts that exploit native control protocols and system utilities inherent to the control-systems ecosystem.
